+/// Secret-SHAPE redaction for agent-authored `bash` command text (issue
+/// #1408 AC3).
+///
+/// The bench autopsy (run 37736364517, `configure-git-webserver`) recorded
+/// the agent's own words: *"The literal key filename got mangled by a
+/// filter — I'll use a different key name."* A filter had rewritten text
+/// inside a FILENAME the agent was creating; the agent discovered the
+/// corruption via I/O errors and planned around a filesystem being edited
+/// under it.
+///
+/// The contract after the fix:
+///
+/// - ONLY a recognized secret SHAPE — a vendor token regex match (AWS
+///   `AKIA…`, GitHub `ghp_…`, OpenAI `sk-…`, JWT, …) — is ever rewritten.
+///   Key-like text that matches no shape (random filenames, entropy-heavy
+///   identifiers, hex runs) stays byte-identical: agent-authored command
+///   text is never touched on a heuristic.
+/// - Every forced rewrite produces a [BashCommandRewrite.notice] naming
+///   exactly what changed; the bash tool surfaces it in the tool result so
+///   the agent sees the rewrite instead of discovering it by failure.
+///
+/// Pure and synchronous: [layerVendor] does the detection, this module only
+/// slices the command around the (non-overlapping, position-sorted)
+/// matches.
+library;
+
+import '../redact/layer_vendor.dart';
+import '../redact/redaction_types.dart';
+
+/// One rewritten span: the matched secret shape and where it sat in the
+/// ORIGINAL command text.
+final class BashCommandShapeChange {
+  /// The change record.
+  const BashCommandShapeChange({
+    required this.label,
+    required this.start,
+    required this.end,
+  });
+
+  /// The vendor kind label (e.g. `AWS Access Key`) — the name the notice
+  /// reports.
+  final String label;
+
+  /// Start offset of the original span.
+  final int start;
+
+  /// End offset (exclusive) of the original span.
+  final int end;
+}
+
+/// A rewritten bash command plus the record of every span that changed.
+final class BashCommandRewrite {
+  /// The rewrite result: [command] is what must execute/persist.
+  const BashCommandRewrite({required this.command, required this.changes});
+
+  /// The command text with every recognized secret shape replaced by its
+  /// `[REDACTED:<kind>]` marker.
+  final String command;
+
+  /// Every rewrite, in command order.
+  final List<BashCommandShapeChange> changes;
+
+  /// The tool-result notice naming exactly what changed (issue #1408 AC3):
+  /// count plus every rewritten shape's label, in order.
+  String get notice {
+    final labels = changes.map((change) => change.label).join(', ');
+    final n = changes.length;
+    return '[bash interceptor rewrote $n secret-shaped value'
+        '${n == 1 ? '' : 's'} in the command ($labels) — the executed '
+        'command carries the [REDACTED:…] markers; agent-authored text '
+        'that is not a recognized secret shape is never rewritten. Pass '
+        'the value as an env var (\$NAME) instead of literal text, or '
+        'register it with request_secret to have it passed verbatim.]';
+  }
+}
+
+/// Rewrites every recognized secret SHAPE in [command], or null when the
+/// command matches none — the common case, and the guarantee: key-like
+/// text without a full shape (filenames, identifiers) is never rewritten.
+///
+/// [config] selects the vendor layer (default: enabled, like the
+/// pipeline); a master-disabled config (`redact.enabled: false`) or one
+/// with the vendor layer off yields null — the same `redact:` section
+/// steers command rewriting and result/job-log masking (review
+/// 5456649624).
+///
+/// [approvedLiterals] are values the host registered as secrets (the
+/// `request_secret` tool, preconfig API keys → the pipeline's
+/// `registeredSecrets`): a match whose original text is one of them is
+/// left byte-identical so an approved value still materializes (the
+/// pipeline already masks it in transcripts). Without this escape hatch a
+/// credential-setup task would have no bash path for its own token
+/// (review 5456649624).
+BashCommandRewrite? redactBashCommandSecretShapes(
+  String command, {
+  RedactionConfig config = const RedactionConfig(),
+  Set<String> approvedLiterals = const {},
+}) {
+  final trimmed = command.trim();
+  if (trimmed.isEmpty ||
+      !config.enabled ||
+      !config.isLayerEnabled(RedactionLayer.vendor)) {
+    return null;
+  }
+  // layerVendor returns non-overlapping matches, but grouped per pattern —
+  // sort by position before slicing. Copy-free: on a quick-screen miss the
+  // layer returns a CONST (unmodifiable) empty list, so the emptiness check
+  // must precede any sort (issue #1408 red-head: sorting the const list
+  // crashed every bash call without a vendor-shaped substring).
+  final matches = layerVendor(command, config);
+  if (matches.isEmpty) return null;
+  matches.sort((a, b) => a.start.compareTo(b.start));
+  if (approvedLiterals.isNotEmpty) {
+    matches.removeWhere(
+      (match) => approvedLiterals.contains(
+        command.substring(match.start, match.end),
+      ),
+    );
+    if (matches.isEmpty) return null;
+  }
+  final buffer = StringBuffer();
+  final changes = <BashCommandShapeChange>[];
+  var cursor = 0;
+  for (final match in matches) {
+    buffer
+      ..write(command.substring(cursor, match.start))
+      ..write(redactionMarker(match.kindLabel));
+    changes.add(
+      BashCommandShapeChange(
+        label: match.kindLabel,
+        start: match.start,
+        end: match.end,
+      ),
+    );
+    cursor = match.end;
+  }
+  buffer.write(command.substring(cursor));
+  return BashCommandRewrite(command: buffer.toString(), changes: changes);
+}

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1410
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1410
- **Title**: fix(1408): harness-induced bench failures — isolated job logs, redacted at rest, shape-only bash interceptor (AC1–AC3; AC4 documented)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1408-bench-harness-artifacts` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 27
- **Additions**: +1116
- **Deletions**: -29
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T11:25:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T20:46:35Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1408 (harness ACs). Bench-autopsy r3, run 37736364517: **~half of the non-stall failures were harness-induced, not agent failures.** This PR fixes the harness side (AC1–AC3) and root-causes AC4 with no code change, as the AC directs.

## AC1 — bench/unattended artifacts leave the task workspace
Evidence (H1, CONFIRMED ×2): `sanitize-git-repo`/`.hard` passed both secret tests and failed ONLY `test_no_other_files_changed` — fa's bash-job logs at `<task-cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs/` captured raw secrets from the agent's own greps; the agent sanitized its own harness logs; the extra modified files flipped the graded diff. The session root was already outside (`--session-root /agent-logs|/logs/agent/fah-sessions`); job logs were not.

- `ShellJobRegistry.jobLogDir` (default unchanged: `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs`), resolved at boot from `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR` (`jobLogDirOverride`; lib/ stays dart:io-free, the executable passes `Platform.environment`).
- The terminal-bench and harbor adapters export `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR=/tmp/fa-harness-artifacts/bash_jobs` — the in-container twin of $RUNNER_TEMP (pinned by a python UT on both adapters' env).
- UT: a run with the override leaves **no `.fah/` in the task dir** after completion; default location pinned for compat.

## AC2 — job logs redacted at rest
Evidence (H1): the logs are documented as NOT redacted and leaked real dataset secrets onto shared runners. Every detached job's log writes now pass through a line-buffered `JobLogRedactor` (new, `lib/src/env/`) **before** the size ceiling, so the resting file carries `[REDACTED:<kind>]` markers; a secret split across stream chunks still masks and the settle path flushes the trailing partial line. The CLI wires the same `RedactionPipeline` that masks tool results into the registry; the option forwards through every options rewrap (secrets/session-vars/cwd decorators, cube sandbox). The live output stream stays raw (transient; feeds the password detector) — at-rest is the contract, and `bash_job output` tails the redacted file.

- UTs: registry-level and LocalShell-level — a job echoing a fixture AWS access key leaves the marker on disk, never the secret; registered non-vendor secrets mask; no-redactor hosts keep byte-identical logs.

## AC3 — the interceptor never rewrites agent-authored identifiers
Evidence (H2, CONFIRMED): `configure-git-webserver` — the transcript records *"The literal key filename got mangled by a filter — I'll use a different key name."* A filter rewrote text inside a FILENAME the agent was creating; the agent found out via I/O errors.

- New `redactBashCommandSecretShapes` (`lib/src/approval/bash_shape_redaction.dart`): **only a recognized secret SHAPE** — a vendor token regex match (AWS `AKIA+16`, GitHub `ghp_`, OpenAI `sk-`, JWT, …) — is ever rewritten to `[REDACTED:<kind>]`. Key-like-but-unmatched text (random filenames, entropy-heavy identifiers, hex runs) stays byte-identical: no heuristic ever mutates agent-authored command text.
- The bash tool executes the rewritten command and prefixes the tool result with a notice **naming exactly what changed** (count + every shape label) on all three paths (foreground, yield-job, background) — the agent sees the rewrite instead of discovering corruption by failure.
- UTs: (a) a command creating a file whose name contains a key-like token is NOT rewritten (and runs byte-identically, no notice); (b) a true secret shape IS rewritten and the notice names it.

## AC4 — H4 root cause: no propagation bug; prompt-contract candidate (no code, per the AC)
Traced the full env path for the `create-bucket` trial: `LocalShell._environment` = `{...Platform.environment, ...?given}` — ambient env is inherited, `ShellExecOptions.env` overrides, never replaces (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`; pinned by the existing UT `env overrides merge over the host environment` in `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`). Every decorator (secrets, session-vars, cwd) merges additively; the bash tool passes no env; the adapters launch fa via docker-exec/tmux inside the task container, so compose-level task env reaches fa's process and its bash children. There is no env filtering/allowlist anywhere in the exec path. Conclusion: the creds the agent failed to find were **genuinely absent from that trial's container** (agent checked `aws configure list` + env, asked via request_secret, was declined unattended, stopped cleanly) — a task-side provisioning gap, not an fa bug. Documented as a **prompt-contract candidate**: "hunt credentials in common places (~/.aws/, /run/secrets/*, task files, metadata endpoints, localstack endpoint env) before declaring them missing", pairing with #1407's repeat-unresolved audit (H3's crashing test belongs there too).

## Tests
TDD; test files mirror lib/ structure (`test/approval/bash_shape_redaction_test.dart`, `test/tools/shell_jobs_isolation_test.dart`, groups in `test/env/shell_job_io_test.dart`, `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest` in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`). New code stays well under the 2800-line ceiling (largest touched file 1333 lines) and every new method is small (CC ≤ 8) and covered. Python suite: 234 tests, 1 pre-existing env failure unrelated to this branch (`test_sitecustomize` needs py≥3.10 `assertNoLogs`). Dart VM is unavailable in this lane (SIGKILLed) — changes verified by close reading; the gate re-runs in CI.

Fixes #1408

+/// Secret-SHAPE redaction for agent-authored `bash` command text (issue
+/// #1408 AC3).
+///
+/// The bench autopsy (run 37736364517, `configure-git-webserver`) recorded
+/// the agent's own words: *"The literal key filename got mangled by a
+/// filter — I'll use a different key name."* A filter had rewritten text
+/// inside a FILENAME the agent was creating; the agent discovered the
+/// corruption via I/O errors and planned around a filesystem being edited
+/// under it.
+///
+/// The contract after the fix:
+///
+/// - ONLY a recognized secret SHAPE — a vendor token regex match (AWS
+///   `AKIA…`, GitHub `ghp_…`, OpenAI `sk-…`, JWT, …) — is ever rewritten.
+///   Key-like text that matches no shape (random filenames, entropy-heavy
+///   identifiers, hex runs) stays byte-identical: agent-authored command
+///   text is never touched on a heuristic.
+/// - Every forced rewrite produces a [BashCommandRewrite.notice] naming
+///   exactly what changed; the bash tool surfaces it in the tool result so
+///   the agent sees the rewrite instead of discovering it by failure.
+///
+/// Pure and synchronous: [layerVendor] does the detection, this module only
+/// slices the command around the (non-overlapping, position-sorted)
+/// matches.
+library;
+
+import '../redact/layer_vendor.dart';
+import '../redact/redaction_types.dart';
+
+/// One rewritten span: the matched secret shape and where it sat in the
+/// ORIGINAL command text.
+final class BashCommandShapeChange {
+  /// The change record.
+  const BashCommandShapeChange({
+    required this.label,
+    required this.start,
+    required this.end,
+  });
+
+  /// The vendor kind label (e.g. `AWS Access Key`) — the name the notice
+  /// reports.
+  final String label;
+
+  /// Start offset of the original span.
+  final int start;
+
+  /// End offset (exclusive) of the original span.
+  final int end;
+}
+
+/// A rewritten bash command plus the record of every span that changed.
+final class BashCommandRewrite {
+  /// The rewrite result: [command] is what must execute/persist.
+  const BashCommandRewrite({required this.command, required this.changes});
+
+  /// The command text with every recognized secret shape replaced by its
+  /// `[REDACTED:<kind>]` marker.
+  final String command;
+
+  /// Every rewrite, in command order.
+  final List<BashCommandShapeChange> changes;
+
+  /// The tool-result notice naming exactly what changed (issue #1408 AC3):
+  /// count plus every rewritten shape's label, in order.
+  String get notice {
+    final labels = changes.map((change) => change.label).join(', ');
+    final n = changes.length;
+    return '[bash interceptor rewrote $n secret-shaped value'
+        '${n == 1 ? '' : 's'} in the command ($labels) — the executed '
+        'command carries the [REDACTED:…] markers; agent-authored text '
+        'that is not a recognized secret shape is never rewritten. Pass '
+        'the value as an env var (\$NAME) instead of literal text, or '
+        'register it with request_secret to have it passed verbatim.]';
+  }
+}
+
+/// Rewrites every recognized secret SHAPE in [command], or null when the
+/// command matches none — the common case, and the guarantee: key-like
+/// text without a full shape (filenames, identifiers) is never rewritten.
+///
+/// [config] selects the vendor layer (default: enabled, like the
+/// pipeline); a master-disabled config (`redact.enabled: false`) or one
+/// with the vendor layer off yields null — the same `redact:` section
+/// steers command rewriting and result/job-log masking (review
+/// 5456649624).
+///
+/// [approvedLiterals] are values the host registered as secrets (the
+/// `request_secret` tool, preconfig API keys → the pipeline's
+/// `registeredSecrets`): a match whose original text is one of them is
+/// left byte-identical so an approved value still materializes (the
+/// pipeline already masks it in transcripts). Without this escape hatch a
+/// credential-setup task would have no bash path for its own token
+/// (review 5456649624).
+BashCommandRewrite? redactBashCommandSecretShapes(
+  String command, {
+  RedactionConfig config = const RedactionConfig(),
+  Set<String> approvedLiterals = const {},
+}) {
+  final trimmed = command.trim();
+  if (trimmed.isEmpty ||
+      !config.enabled ||
+      !config.isLayerEnabled(RedactionLayer.vendor)) {
+    return null;
+  }
+  // layerVendor returns non-overlapping matches, but grouped per pattern —
+  // sort by position before slicing. Copy-free: on a quick-screen miss the
+  // layer returns a CONST (unmodifiable) empty list, so the emptiness check
+  // must precede any sort (issue #1408 red-head: sorting the const list
+  // crashed every bash call without a vendor-shaped substring).
+  final matches = layerVendor(command, config);
+  if (matches.isEmpty) return null;
+  matches.sort((a, b) => a.start.compareTo(b.start));
+  if (approvedLiterals.isNotEmpty) {
+    matches.removeWhere(
+      (match) => approvedLiterals.contains(
+        command.substring(match.start, match.end),
+      ),
+    );
+    if (matches.isEmpty) return null;
+  }
+  final buffer = StringBuffer();
+  final changes = <BashCommandShapeChange>[];
+  var cursor = 0;
+  for (final match in matches) {
+    buffer
+      ..write(command.substring(cursor, match.start))
+      ..write(redactionMarker(match.kindLabel));
+    changes.add(
+      BashCommandShapeChange(
+        label: match.kindLabel,
+        start: match.start,
+        end: match.end,
+      ),
+    );
+    cursor = match.end;
+  }
+  buffer.write(command.substring(cursor));
+  return BashCommandRewrite(command: buffer.toString(), changes: changes);
+}

This is a re-review cycle. The previous review (REQUEST_CHANGES) raised:
1. 🚨 BLOCKING: bash tool crash on sort of const [] — author claims fixed in 47b5356d1 (sort-guard: check isEmpty before sort)
2. 🚨 BLOCKING: test file doesn't compile — author claims fixed in 93ad382a4

4. ⚠️ IMPORTANT: config-blind rewrite + no escape hatch — author claims fixed in f604134d6 (redactionConfig param + approvedSecretLiterals)
5. ⚠️ IMPORTANT: unbounded carry — author claims fixed in d6bf6a1f4 (1 MiB cap)
6. 💡 SUGGESTION: notice before truncation — author claims fixed in f604134d6
7. 💡 SUGGESTION: marker duplication — author claims fixed in f604134d6 (redactionMarker helper)
8. 💡 SUGGESTION: harbor adapter hardcoded path — author claims fixed in 9e1d8771a (_CONTAINER_JOB_LOG_DIR)
9. Non-blocking: flutter_app AgentService doesn't wire jobLogRedactor (AC2 parity) — is this fixed? Let me check.

My job now: verify all these fixes are actually present in the current diff, look for new issues, and produce the verdict. Let me verify each claim in the current checkout:

1. Sort-guard: VERIFIED in current code — `matches.isEmpty` check happens before `matches.sort`. And the comment says layerVendor returns const [] on quick-screen miss. But wait — is the list returned on a NON-miss (matches found) growable? `matches.sort` on a non-const list is fine if it's growable. Let me check layerVendor to see what it returns when there ARE matches — if it returns a `List.unmodifiable` or a const list in some other path, sort would still crash. Let me check layer_vendor.dart.

2. Analyzer issues in test file: current test file shows `String _textOf(...)` — fixed. `Result<ShellExecResult, ExecutionError> result = const Ok(...)` — fixed.

3. CLI bookkeeping: `_jobBookkeepingDir` getter now used for `_manifestPath`, `_withRegistryLock`, `_pruneOldJobLogs`. Fixed. But I should double-check: are there other places hardcoding `.fah/bash_jobs` in the CLI path? E.g., `captureLostJobs`, hub-mode `jobStarted`? The author says hub-mode jobStarted writes through the same `_manifestPath`. Let me grep.

4. redactionConfig + approvedSecretLiterals — verified in the diff above.

5. _maxCarryBytes cap — verified in job_log_redaction.dart.

6. Notice after truncation — verified in the diff (the `_awaitJobOutcome` change).

7. redactionMarker helper — verified in redaction_types.dart, used by pipeline and shape rewriter.

8. harbor _CONTAINER_JOB_LOG_DIR — verified in the diff.

9. flutter_app AgentService — need to check if it wires jobLogRedactor.

Then do my own fresh review of the current head for NEW issues:

Things to scrutinize:
a. `JobLogRedactor.ingest` — the overflow path: `_carry = ''` then `return transform(buffered) + _overflowMarker;`. Note buffered here is _carry + chunk. This force-flushes EVERYTHING including complete lines... fine, best-effort documented.

But there's a subtle issue: in the overflow path when `cut >= 0`? No wait — overflow only handled in the `cut < 0` branch. If buffered has a newline and is huge, the carry (`substring(cut+1)`) is bounded by the last line length — but a single line can still be > 1 MiB! Wait: if `cut >= 0`, `_carry = buffered.substring(cut + 1)` — that's the trailing partial line, which could be arbitrarily long if the chunk contains a newline early and then megabytes of text without another newline. Next ingest call: buffered = _carry (1 MiB+) + chunk... if again no newline, eventually > 1 MiB → force-flush. OK so the bound is enforced on the NEXT ingest, meaning the carry can temporarily exceed 1 MiB within a single ingest call (e.g., a chunk of 100 MiB containing a newline at position 0 and no more newlines: cut=0, carry = 100 MiB, returned). Hmm — the carry itself can exceed _maxCarryBytes after a single ingest. The force-flush only happens on the NEXT ingest call when there's no newline. Also at flush() time, the whole carry is transformed and returned — the return value flows into `_ceiling.ingest(rest)` which is a string in memory anyway. The memory bound: carry ≤ chunk size + prior carry. The chunk itself is already in memory (it came from the stream), so ingest doesn't grow memory beyond ~2x chunk size in the worst case within one call... Actually wait, no: carry grows ACROSS chunks. Each ingest concatenates _carry + chunk. If a job streams newline-free chunks of 64 KiB each, after 16 chunks buffered = 1 MiB → force-flush on the 17th. So the bound holds across chunks (carry ≤ 1 MiB + one chunk). Except the case above where a single chunk contains a newline followed by a huge tail — carry can be as big as one chunk. That's inherent (the chunk is already in memory), acceptable.

b. `fanOut` change: `final safe = _logBroken ? chunk : (_redactor?.ingest(chunk) ?? chunk); if (!_logBroken && safe.isNotEmpty)`. 

Subtle issue: if the redactor returns empty string (chunk fully buffered in carry), no write happens — correct. But there's an interplay with the size ceiling: `_ceiling.ingest(safe)` is called per-write. Previously every chunk fed the ceiling; now chunks swallowed by the carry don't. That's fine — bytes counted when actually written.

BUT: what about the ordering between the redactor's transform output and the ceiling's head/tail patching? Redaction shortens text (secrets → markers), so ceiling accounting is on redacted bytes. Fine.

Another subtle thing: the `_writeChain` async ordering vs `_carry` state mutation. `ingest` mutates `_carry` synchronously in fanOut (before the write chain resolves), and `flush()` is called in the settle path after `await _writeChain`. Since ingest is synchronous and always completes before flush (settle happens after streams close), the ordering is safe.

What about TWO concurrent fans? stdout and stderr — are they both routed through fanOut? Let me check the existing code in io_execution_env.dart. If stdout and stderr are separate streams each calling fanOut, and each has its own redactor? No — one shared `_redactor` for the job. Both streams' chunks flow through the same redactor sequentially (single isolate), so interleaving is handled by the line buffering (each chunk is processed atomically). A token split across a stdout-chunk boundary AND stderr interleaving... The carry joins consecutive chunks regardless of source; a secret split between stdout and stderr would be unusual. Fine.

c. The settle flush path: wrapped in try/on Object → `_logBroken = true`. Fine.

d. In `_awaitJobOutcome`, the rewrite notice now rides after truncation — good.

e. `redactBashCommandSecretShapes` — check `layerVendor` returns: the comment claims "on a quick-screen miss the layer returns a CONST (unmodifiable) empty list, so the emptiness check must precede any sort". Need to verify layerVendor's contract: does it ever return an unmodifiable non-empty list? If it returns growable lists per pattern merged... let me read layer_vendor.dart.

f. The `approvedLiterals` check uses `command.substring(match.start, match.end)` — exact-value comparison against registered secrets. Registered secrets are stored... in the pipeline's `registeredSecrets`. The CLI passes `config.redactionPipeline?.registeredSecrets.toSet()`. Is `registeredSecrets` a live list (getter returning unmodifiable view) or a copy? `.toSet()` copies — fine. "Live snapshot" claim: the closure `() => config.redactionPipeline?.registeredSecrets.toSet() ?? const {}` is evaluated per bash call — live. Good.

But one issue: the CLI passes `config.redactionPipeline?.config ?? const RedactionConfig(enabled: false)`. If redactionPipeline is null (redaction off), the config is disabled → no rewriting. If pipeline exists, its config is used. Consistent.

g. Security angle: the interceptor rewrites the command BEFORE execution. That means `echo <aws key>` now echoes the marker. Any false-positive risk: a command legitimately processing example keys (docs, tests) gets mangled — but the notice names it, and this matches the pipeline's existing behavior for results. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1410
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1410
- **Title**: fix(1408): harness-induced bench failures — isolated job logs, redacted at rest, shape-only bash interceptor (AC1–AC3; AC4 documented)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1408-bench-harness-artifacts` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 27
- **Additions**: +1116
- **Deletions**: -29
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T11:25:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T20:46:35Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1408 (harness ACs). Bench-autopsy r3, run 37736364517: **~half of the non-stall failures were harness-induced, not agent failures.** This PR fixes the harness side (AC1–AC3) and root-causes AC4 with no code change, as the AC directs.

## AC1 — bench/unattended artifacts leave the task workspace
Evidence (H1, CONFIRMED ×2): `sanitize-git-repo`/`.hard` passed both secret tests and failed ONLY `test_no_other_files_changed` — fa's bash-job logs at `<task-cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs/` captured raw secrets from the agent's own greps; the agent sanitized its own harness logs; the extra modified files flipped the graded diff. The session root was already outside (`--session-root /agent-logs|/logs/agent/fah-sessions`); job logs were not.

- `ShellJobRegistry.jobLogDir` (default unchanged: `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs`), resolved at boot from `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR` (`jobLogDirOverride`; lib/ stays dart:io-free, the executable passes `Platform.environment`).
- The terminal-bench and harbor adapters export `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR=/tmp/fa-harness-artifacts/bash_jobs` — the in-container twin of $RUNNER_TEMP (pinned by a python UT on both adapters' env).
- UT: a run with the override leaves **no `.fah/` in the task dir** after completion; default location pinned for compat.

## AC2 — job logs redacted at rest
Evidence (H1): the logs are documented as NOT redacted and leaked real dataset secrets onto shared runners. Every detached job's log writes now pass through a line-buffered `JobLogRedactor` (new, `lib/src/env/`) **before** the size ceiling, so the resting file carries `[REDACTED:<kind>]` markers; a secret split across stream chunks still masks and the settle path flushes the trailing partial line. The CLI wires the same `RedactionPipeline` that masks tool results into the registry; the option forwards through every options rewrap (secrets/session-vars/cwd decorators, cube sandbox). The live output stream stays raw (transient; feeds the password detector) — at-rest is the contract, and `bash_job output` tails the redacted file.

- UTs: registry-level and LocalShell-level — a job echoing a fixture AWS access key leaves the marker on disk, never the secret; registered non-vendor secrets mask; no-redactor hosts keep byte-identical logs.

## AC3 — the interceptor never rewrites agent-authored identifiers
Evidence (H2, CONFIRMED): `configure-git-webserver` — the transcript records *"The literal key filename got mangled by a filter — I'll use a different key name."* A filter rewrote text inside a FILENAME the agent was creating; the agent found out via I/O errors.

- New `redactBashCommandSecretShapes` (`lib/src/approval/bash_shape_redaction.dart`): **only a recognized secret SHAPE** — a vendor token regex match (AWS `AKIA+16`, GitHub `ghp_`, OpenAI `sk-`, JWT, …) — is ever rewritten to `[REDACTED:<kind>]`. Key-like-but-unmatched text (random filenames, entropy-heavy identifiers, hex runs) stays byte-identical: no heuristic ever mutates agent-authored command text.
- The bash tool executes the rewritten command and prefixes the tool result with a notice **naming exactly what changed** (count + every shape label) on all three paths (foreground, yield-job, background) — the agent sees the rewrite instead of discovering corruption by failure.
- UTs: (a) a command creating a file whose name contains a key-like token is NOT rewritten (and runs byte-identically, no notice); (b) a true secret shape IS rewritten and the notice names it.

## AC4 — H4 root cause: no propagation bug; prompt-contract candidate (no code, per the AC)
Traced the full env path for the `create-bucket` trial: `LocalShell._environment` = `{...Platform.environment, ...?given}` — ambient env is inherited, `ShellExecOptions.env` overrides, never replaces (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`; pinned by the existing UT `env overrides merge over the host environment` in `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`). Every decorator (secrets, session-vars, cwd) merges additively; the bash tool passes no env; the adapters launch fa via docker-exec/tmux inside the task container, so compose-level task env reaches fa's process and its bash children. There is no env filtering/allowlist anywhere in the exec path. Conclusion: the creds the agent failed to find were **genuinely absent from that trial's container** (agent checked `aws configure list` + env, asked via request_secret, was declined unattended, stopped cleanly) — a task-side provisioning gap, not an fa bug. Documented as a **prompt-contract candidate**: "hunt credentials in common places (~/.aws/, /run/secrets/*, task files, metadata endpoints, localstack endpoint env) before declaring them missing", pairing with #1407's repeat-unresolved audit (H3's crashing test belongs there too).

## Tests
TDD; test files mirror lib/ structure (`test/approval/bash_shape_redaction_test.dart`, `test/tools/shell_jobs_isolation_test.dart`, groups in `test/env/shell_job_io_test.dart`, `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest` in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`). New code stays well under the 2800-line ceiling (largest touched file 1333 lines) and every new method is small (CC ≤ 8) and covered. Python suite: 234 tests, 1 pre-existing env failure unrelated to this branch (`test_sitecustomize` needs py≥3.10 `assertNoLogs`). Dart VM is unavailable in this lane (SIGKILLed) — changes verified by close reading; the gate re-runs in CI.

Fixes #1408

+/// Secret-SHAPE redaction for agent-authored `bash` command text (issue
+/// #1408 AC3).
+///
+/// The bench autopsy (run 37736364517, `configure-git-webserver`) recorded
+/// the agent's own words: *"The literal key filename got mangled by a
+/// filter — I'll use a different key name."* A filter had rewritten text
+/// inside a FILENAME the agent was creating; the agent discovered the
+/// corruption via I/O errors and planned around a filesystem being edited
+/// under it.
+///
+/// The contract after the fix:
+///
+/// - ONLY a recognized secret SHAPE — a vendor token regex match (AWS
+///   `AKIA…`, GitHub `ghp_…`, OpenAI `sk-…`, JWT, …) — is ever rewritten.
+///   Key-like text that matches no shape (random filenames, entropy-heavy
+///   identifiers, hex runs) stays byte-identical: agent-authored command
+///   text is never touched on a heuristic.
+/// - Every forced rewrite produces a [BashCommandRewrite.notice] naming
+///   exactly what changed; the bash tool surfaces it in the tool result so
+///   the agent sees the rewrite instead of discovering it by failure.
+///
+/// Pure and synchronous: [layerVendor] does the detection, this module only
+/// slices the command around the (non-overlapping, position-sorted)
+/// matches.
+library;
+
+import '../redact/layer_vendor.dart';
+import '../redact/redaction_types.dart';
+
+/// One rewritten span: the matched secret shape and where it sat in the
+/// ORIGINAL command text.
+final class BashCommandShapeChange {
+  /// The change record.
+  const BashCommandShapeChange({
+    required this.label,
+    required this.start,
+    required this.end,
+  });
+
+  /// The vendor kind label (e.g. `AWS Access Key`) — the name the notice
+  /// reports.
+  final String label;
+
+  /// Start offset of the original span.
+  final int start;
+
+  /// End offset (exclusive) of the original span.
+  final int end;
+}
+
+/// A rewritten bash command plus the record of every span that changed.
+final class BashCommandRewrite {
+  /// The rewrite result: [command] is what must execute/persist.
+  const BashCommandRewrite({required this.command, required this.changes});
+
+  /// The command text with every recognized secret shape replaced by its
+  /// `[REDACTED:<kind>]` marker.
+  final String command;
+
+  /// Every rewrite, in command order.
+  final List<BashCommandShapeChange> changes;
+
+  /// The tool-result notice naming exactly what changed (issue #1408 AC3):
+  /// count plus every rewritten shape's label, in order.
+  String get notice {
+    final labels = changes.map((change) => change.label).join(', ');
+    final n = changes.length;
+    return '[bash interceptor rewrote $n secret-shaped value'
+        '${n == 1 ? '' : 's'} in the command ($labels) — the executed '
+        'command carries the [REDACTED:…] markers; agent-authored text '
+        'that is not a recognized secret shape is never rewritten. Pass '
+        'the value as an env var (\$NAME) instead of literal text, or '
+        'register it with request_secret to have it passed verbatim.]';
+  }
+}
+
+/// Rewrites every recognized secret SHAPE in [command], or null when the
+/// command matches none — the common case, and the guarantee: key-like
+/// text without a full shape (filenames, identifiers) is never rewritten.
+///
+/// [config] selects the vendor layer (default: enabled, like the
+/// pipeline); a master-disabled config (`redact.enabled: false`) or one
+/// with the vendor layer off yields null — the same `redact:` section
+/// steers command rewriting and result/job-log masking (review
+/// 5456649624).
+///
+/// [approvedLiterals] are values the host registered as secrets (the
+/// `request_secret` tool, preconfig API keys → the pipeline's
+/// `registeredSecrets`): a match whose original text is one of them is
+/// left byte-identical so an approved value still materializes (the
+/// pipeline already masks it in transcripts). Without this escape hatch a
+/// credential-setup task would have no bash path for its own token
+/// (review 5456649624).
+BashCommandRewrite? redactBashCommandSecretShapes(
+  String command, {
+  RedactionConfig config = const RedactionConfig(),
+  Set<String> approvedLiterals = const {},
+}) {
+  final trimmed = command.trim();
+  if (trimmed.isEmpty ||
+      !config.enabled ||
+      !config.isLayerEnabled(RedactionLayer.vendor)) {
+    return null;
+  }
+  // layerVendor returns non-overlapping matches, but grouped per pattern —
+  // sort by position before slicing. Copy-free: on a quick-screen miss the
+  // layer returns a CONST (unmodifiable) empty list, so the emptiness check
+  // must precede any sort (issue #1408 red-head: sorting the const list
+  // crashed every bash call without a vendor-shaped substring).
+  final matches = layerVendor(command, config);
+  if (matches.isEmpty) return null;
+  matches.sort((a, b) => a.start.compareTo(b.start));
+  if (approvedLiterals.isNotEmpty) {
+    matches.removeWhere(
+      (match) => approvedLiterals.contains(
+        command.substring(match.start, match.end),
+      ),
+    );
+    if (matches.isEmpty) return null;
+  }
+  final buffer = StringBuffer();
+  final changes = <BashCommandShapeChange>[];
+  var cursor = 0;
+  for (final match in matches) {
+    buffer
+      ..write(command.substring(cursor, match.start))
+      ..write(redactionMarker(match.kindLabel));
+    changes.add(
+      BashCommandShapeChange(
+        label: match.kindLabel,
+        start: match.start,
+        end: match.end,
+      ),
+    );
+    cursor = match.end;
+  }
+  buffer.write(command.substring(cursor));
+  return BashCommandRewrite(command: buffer.toString(), changes: changes);
+}

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Evidence (H1, CONFIRMED ×2): `sanitize-git-repo`/`.hard` passed both secret tests and failed ONLY `test_no_other_files_changed` — fa's bash-job logs at `<task-cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs/` captured raw secrets from the agent's own greps; the agent sanitized its own harness logs; the extra modified files flipped the graded diff. The session root was already outside (`--session-root /agent-logs|/logs/agent/fah-sessions`); job logs were not.

- `ShellJobRegistry.jobLogDir` (default unchanged: `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs`), resolved at boot from `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR` (`jobLogDirOverride`; lib/ stays dart:io-free, the executable passes `Platform.environment`).
- The terminal-bench and harbor adapters export `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR=/tmp/fa-harness-artifacts/bash_jobs` — the in-container twin of $RUNNER_TEMP (pinned by a python UT on both adapters' env).
- UT: a run with the override leaves **no `.fah/` in the task dir** after completion; default location pinned for compat.

## AC2 — job logs redacted at rest
Evidence (H1): the logs are documented as NOT redacted and leaked real dataset secrets onto shared runners. Every detached job's log writes now pass through a line-buffered `JobLogRedactor` (new, `lib/src/env/`) **before** the size ceiling, so the resting file carries `[REDACTED:<kind>]` markers; a secret split across stream chunks still masks and the settle path flushes the trailing partial line. The CLI wires the same `RedactionPipeline` that masks tool results into the registry; the option forwards through every options rewrap (secrets/session-vars/cwd decorators, cube sandbox). The live output stream stays raw (transient; feeds the password detector) — at-rest is the contract, and `bash_job output` tails the redacted file.

- UTs: registry-level and LocalShell-level — a job echoing a fixture AWS access key leaves the marker on disk, never the secret; registered non-vendor secrets mask; no-redactor hosts keep byte-identical logs.

## AC3 — the interceptor never rewrites agent-authored identifiers
Evidence (H2, CONFIRMED): `configure-git-webserver` — the transcript records *"The literal key filename got mangled by a filter — I'll use a different key name."* A filter rewrote text inside a FILENAME the agent was creating; the agent found out via I/O errors.

- New `redactBashCommandSecretShapes` (`lib/src/approval/bash_shape_redaction.dart`): **only a recognized secret SHAPE** — a vendor token regex match (AWS `AKIA+16`, GitHub `ghp_`, OpenAI `sk-`, JWT, …) — is ever rewritten to `[REDACTED:<kind>]`. Key-like-but-unmatched text (random filenames, entropy-heavy identifiers, hex runs) stays byte-identical: no heuristic ever mutates agent-authored command text.
- The bash tool executes the rewritten command and prefixes the tool result with a notice **naming exactly what changed** (count + every shape label) on all three paths (foreground, yield-job, background) — the agent sees the rewrite instead of discovering corruption by failure.
- UTs: (a) a command creating a file whose name contains a key-like token is NOT rewritten (and runs byte-identically, no notice); (b) a true secret shape IS rewritten and the notice names it.

## AC4 — H4 root cause: no propagation bug; prompt-contract candidate (no code, per the AC)
Traced the full env path for the `create-bucket` trial: `LocalShell._environment` = `{...Platform.environment, ...?given}` — ambient env is inherited, `ShellExecOptions.env` overrides, never replaces (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`; pinned by the existing UT `env overrides merge over the host environment` in `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`). Every decorator (secrets, session-vars, cwd) merges additively; the bash tool passes no env; the adapters launch fa via docker-exec/tmux inside the task container, so compose-level task env reaches fa's process and its bash children. There is no env filtering/allowlist anywhere in the exec path. Conclusion: the creds the agent failed to find were **genuinely absent from that trial's container** (agent checked `aws configure list` + env, asked via request_secret, was declined unattended, stopped cleanly) — a task-side provisioning gap, not an fa bug. Documented as a **prompt-contract candidate**: "hunt credentials in common places (~/.aws/, /run/secrets/*, task files, metadata endpoints, localstack endpoint env) before declaring them missing", pairing with #1407's repeat-unresolved audit (H3's crashing test belongs there too).

## Tests
TDD; test files mirror lib/ structure (`test/approval/bash_shape_redaction_test.dart`, `test/tools/shell_jobs_isolation_test.dart`, groups in `test/env/shell_job_io_test.dart`, `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest` in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`). New code stays well under the 2800-line ceiling (largest touched file 1333 lines) and every new method is small (CC ≤ 8) and covered. Python suite: 234 tests, 1 pre-existing env failure unrelated to this branch (`test_sitecustomize` needs py≥3.10 `assertNoLogs`). Dart VM is unavailable in this lane (SIGKILLed) — changes verified by close reading; the gate re-runs in CI.

Fixes #1408

+/// Secret-SHAPE redaction for agent-authored `bash` command text (issue
+/// #1408 AC3).
+///
+/// The bench autopsy (run 37736364517, `configure-git-webserver`) recorded
+/// the agent's own words: *"The literal key filename got mangled by a
+/// filter — I'll use a different key name."* A filter had rewritten text
+/// inside a FILENAME the agent was creating; the agent discovered the
+/// corruption via I/O errors and planned around a filesystem being edited
+/// under it.
+///
+/// The contract after the fix:
+///
+/// - ONLY a recognized secret SHAPE — a vendor token regex match (AWS
+///   `AKIA…`, GitHub `ghp_…`, OpenAI `sk-…`, JWT, …) — is ever rewritten.
+///   Key-like text that matches no shape (random filenames, entropy-heavy
+///   identifiers, hex runs) stays byte-identical: agent-authored command
+///   text is never touched on a heuristic.
+/// - Every forced rewrite produces a [BashCommandRewrite.notice] naming
+///   exactly what changed; the bash tool surfaces it in the tool result so
+///   the agent sees the rewrite instead of discovering it by failure.
+///
+/// Pure and synchronous: [layerVendor] does the detection, this module only
+/// slices the command around the (non-overlapping, position-sorted)
+/// matches.
+library;
+
+import '../redact/layer_vendor.dart';
+import '../redact/redaction_types.dart';
+
+/// One rewritten span: the matched secret shape and where it sat in the
+/// ORIGINAL command text.
+final class BashCommandShapeChange {
+  /// The change record.
+  const BashCommandShapeChange({
+    required this.label,
+    required this.start,
+    required this.end,
+  });
+
+  /// The vendor kind label (e.g. `AWS Access Key`) — the name the notice
+  /// reports.
+  final String label;
+
+  /// Start offset of the original span.
+  final int start;
+
+  /// End offset (exclusive) of the original span.
+  final int end;
+}
+
+/// A rewritten bash command plus the record of every span that changed.
+final class BashCommandRewrite {
+  /// The rewrite result: [command] is what must execute/persist.
+  const BashCommandRewrite({required this.command, required this.changes});
+
+  /// The command text with every recognized secret shape replaced by its
+  /// `[REDACTED:<kind>]` marker.
+  final String command;
+
+  /// Every rewrite, in command order.
+  final List<BashCommandShapeChange> changes;
+
+  /// The tool-result notice naming exactly what changed (issue #1408 AC3):
+  /// count plus every rewritten shape's label, in order.
+  String get notice {
+    final labels = changes.map((change) => change.label).join(', ');
+    final n = changes.length;
+    return '[bash interceptor rewrote $n secret-shaped value'
+        '${n == 1 ? '' : 's'} in the command ($labels) — the executed '
+        'command carries the [REDACTED:…] markers; agent-authored text '
+        'that is not a recognized secret shape is never rewritten. Pass '
+        'the value as an env var (\$NAME) instead of literal text, or '
+        'register it with request_secret to have it passed verbatim.]';
+  }
+}
+
+/// Rewrites every recognized secret SHAPE in [command], or null when the
+/// command matches none — the common case, and the guarantee: key-like
+/// text without a full shape (filenames, identifiers) is never rewritten.
+///
+/// [config] selects the vendor layer (default: enabled, like the
+/// pipeline); a master-disabled config (`redact.enabled: false`) or one
+/// with the vendor layer off yields null — the same `redact:` section
+/// steers command rewriting and result/job-log masking (review
+/// 5456649624).
+///
+/// [approvedLiterals] are values the host registered as secrets (the
+/// `request_secret` tool, preconfig API keys → the pipeline's
+/// `registeredSecrets`): a match whose original text is one of them is
+/// left byte-identical so an approved value still materializes (the
+/// pipeline already masks it in transcripts). Without this escape hatch a
+/// credential-setup task would have no bash path for its own token
+/// (review 5456649624).
+BashCommandRewrite? redactBashCommandSecretShapes(
+  String command, {
+  RedactionConfig config = const RedactionConfig(),
+  Set<String> approvedLiterals = const {},
+}) {
+  final trimmed = command.trim();
+  if (trimmed.isEmpty ||
+      !config.enabled ||
+      !config.isLayerEnabled(RedactionLayer.vendor)) {
+    return null;
+  }
+  // layerVendor returns non-overlapping matches, but grouped per pattern —
+  // sort by position before slicing. Copy-free: on a quick-screen miss the
+  // layer returns a CONST (unmodifiable) empty list, so the emptiness check
+  // must precede any sort (issue #1408 red-head: sorting the const list
+  // crashed every bash call without a vendor-shaped substring).
+  final matches = layerVendor(command, config);
+  if (matches.isEmpty) return null;
+  matches.sort((a, b) => a.start.compareTo(b.start));
+  if (approvedLiterals.isNotEmpty) {
+    matches.removeWhere(
+      (match) => approvedLiterals.contains(
+        command.substring(match.start, match.end),
+      ),
+    );
+    if (matches.isEmpty) return null;
+  }
+  final buffer = StringBuffer();
+  final changes = <BashCommandShapeChange>[];
+  var cursor = 0;
+  for (final match in matches) {
+    buffer
+      ..write(command.substring(cursor, match.start))
+      ..write(redactionMarker(match.kindLabel));
+    changes.add(
+      BashCommandShapeChange(
+        label: match.kindLabel,
+        start: match.start,
+        end: match.end,
+      ),
+    );
+    cursor = match.end;
+  }
+  buffer.write(command.substring(cursor));
+  return BashCommandRewrite(command: buffer.toString(), changes: changes);
+}

This is a re-review cycle. The previous review (REQUEST_CHANGES) raised:
1. 🚨 BLOCKING: bash tool crash on sort of const [] — author claims fixed in 47b5356d1 (sort-guard: check isEmpty before sort)
2. 🚨 BLOCKING: test file doesn't compile — author claims fixed in 93ad382a4
3. 🚨 BLOCKING: AC1 CLI bookkeeping gap — author claims fixed in 9e1d8771a (`_jobBookkeepingDir` getter)
4. ⚠️ IMPORTANT: config-blind rewrite + no escape hatch — author claims fixed in f604134d6 (redactionConfig param + approvedSecretLiterals)
5. ⚠️ IMPORTANT: unbounded carry — author claims fixed in d6bf6a1f4 (1 MiB cap)
6. 💡 SUGGESTION: notice before truncation — author claims fixed in f604134d6
7. 💡 SUGGESTION: marker duplication — author claims fixed in f604134d6 (redactionMarker helper)
8. 💡 SUGGESTION: harbor adapter hardcoded path — author claims fixed in 9e1d8771a (_CONTAINER_JOB_LOG_DIR)
9. Non-blocking: flutter_app AgentService doesn't wire jobLogRedactor (AC2 parity) — is this fixed? Let me check.

My job now: verify all these fixes are actually present in the current diff, look for new issues, and produce the verdict. Let me verify each claim in the current checkout:

1. Sort-guard: VERIFIED in current code — `matches.isEmpty` check happens before `matches.sort`. And the comment says layerVendor returns const [] on quick-screen miss. But wait — is the list returned on a NON-miss (matches found) growable? `matches.sort` on a non-const list is fine if it's growable. Let me check layerVendor to see what it returns when there ARE matches — if it returns a `List.unmodifiable` or a const list in some other path, sort would still crash. Let me check layer_vendor.dart.

2. Analyzer issues in test file: current test file shows `String _textOf(...)` — fixed. `Result<ShellExecResult, ExecutionError> result = const Ok(...)` — fixed.

3. CLI bookkeeping: `_jobBookkeepingDir` getter now used for `_manifestPath`, `_withRegistryLock`, `_pruneOldJobLogs`. Fixed. But I should double-check: are there other places hardcoding `.fah/bash_jobs` in the CLI path? E.g., `captureLostJobs`, hub-mode `jobStarted`? The author says hub-mode jobStarted writes through the same `_manifestPath`. Let me grep.

4. redactionConfig + approvedSecretLiterals — verified in the diff above.

5. _maxCarryBytes cap — verified in job_log_redaction.dart.

6. Notice after truncation — verified in the diff (the `_awaitJobOutcome` change).

7. redactionMarker helper — verified in redaction_types.dart, used by pipeline and shape rewriter.

8. harbor _CONTAINER_JOB_LOG_DIR — verified in the diff.

9. flutter_app AgentService — need to check if it wires jobLogRedactor.

Then do my own fresh review of the current head for NEW issues:

Things to scrutinize:
a. `JobLogRedactor.ingest` — the overflow path: `_carry = ''` then `return transform(buffered) + _overflowMarker;`. Note buffered here is _carry + chunk. This force-flushes EVERYTHING including complete lines... fine, best-effort documented.

But there's a subtle issue: in the overflow path when `cut >= 0`? No wait — overflow only handled in the `cut < 0` branch. If buffered has a newline and is huge, the carry (`substring(cut+1)`) is bounded by the last line length — but a single line can still be > 1 MiB! Wait: if `cut >= 0`, `_carry = buffered.substring(cut + 1)` — that's the trailing partial line, which could be arbitrarily long if the chunk contains a newline early and then megabytes of text without another newline. Next ingest call: buffered = _carry (1 MiB+) + chunk... if again no newline, eventually > 1 MiB → force-flush. OK so the bound is enforced on the NEXT ingest, meaning the carry can temporarily exceed 1 MiB within a single ingest call (e.g., a chunk of 100 MiB containing a newline at position 0 and no more newlines: cut=0, carry = 100 MiB, returned). Hmm — the carry itself can exceed _maxCarryBytes after a single ingest. The force-flush only happens on the NEXT ingest call when there's no newline. Also at flush() time, the whole carry is transformed and returned — the return value flows into `_ceiling.ingest(rest)` which is a string in memory anyway. The memory bound: carry ≤ chunk size + prior carry. The chunk itself is already in memory (it came from the stream), so ingest doesn't grow memory beyond ~2x chunk size in the worst case within one call... Actually wait, no: carry grows ACROSS chunks. Each ingest concatenates _carry + chunk. If a job streams newline-free chunks of 64 KiB each, after 16 chunks buffered = 1 MiB → force-flush on the 17th. So the bound holds across chunks (carry ≤ 1 MiB + one chunk). Except the case above where a single chunk contains a newline followed by a huge tail — carry can be as big as one chunk. That's inherent (the chunk is already in memory), acceptable.

b. `fanOut` change: `final safe = _logBroken ? chunk : (_redactor?.ingest(chunk) ?? chunk); if (!_logBroken && safe.isNotEmpty)`. 

Subtle issue: if the redactor returns empty string (chunk fully buffered in carry), no write happens — correct. But there's an interplay with the size ceiling: `_ceiling.ingest(safe)` is called per-write. Previously every chunk fed the ceiling; now chunks swallowed by the carry don't. That's fine — bytes counted when actually written.

BUT: what about the ordering between the redactor's transform output and the ceiling's head/tail patching? Redaction shortens text (secrets → markers), so ceiling accounting is on redacted bytes. Fine.

Another subtle thing: the `_writeChain` async ordering vs `_carry` state mutation. `ingest` mutates `_carry` synchronously in fanOut (before the write chain resolves), and `flush()` is called in the settle path after `await _writeChain`. Since ingest is synchronous and always completes before flush (settle happens after streams close), the ordering is safe.

What about TWO concurrent fans? stdout and stderr — are they both routed through fanOut? Let me check the existing code in io_execution_env.dart. If stdout and stderr are separate streams each calling fanOut, and each has its own redactor? No — one shared `_redactor` for the job. Both streams' chunks flow through the same redactor sequentially (single isolate), so interleaving is handled by the line buffering (each chunk is processed atomically). A token split across a stdout-chunk boundary AND stderr interleaving... The carry joins consecutive chunks regardless of source; a secret split between stdout and stderr would be unusual. Fine.

c. The settle flush path: wrapped in try/on Object → `_logBroken = true`. Fine.

d. In `_awaitJobOutcome`, the rewrite notice now rides after truncation — good.

e. `redactBashCommandSecretShapes` — check `layerVendor` returns: the comment claims "on a quick-screen miss the layer returns a CONST (unmodifiable) empty list, so the emptiness check must precede any sort". Need to verify layerVendor's contract: does it ever return an unmodifiable non-empty list? If it returns growable lists per pattern merged... let me read layer_vendor.dart.

f. The `approvedLiterals` check uses `command.substring(match.start, match.end)` — exact-value comparison against registered secrets. Registered secrets are stored... in the pipeline's `registeredSecrets`. The CLI passes `config.redactionPipeline?.registeredSecrets.toSet()`. Is `registeredSecrets` a live list (getter returning unmodifiable view) or a copy? `.toSet()` copies — fine. "Live snapshot" claim: the closure `() => config.redactionPipeline?.registeredSecrets.toSet() ?? const {}` is evaluated per bash call — live. Good.

But one issue: the CLI passes `config.redactionPipeline?.config ?? const RedactionConfig(enabled: false)`. If redactionPipeline is null (redaction off), the config is disabled → no rewriting. If pipeline exists, its config is used. Consistent.

g. Security angle: the interceptor rewrites the command BEFORE execution. That means `echo <aws key>` now echoes the marker. Any false-positive risk: a command legitimately processing example keys (docs, tests) gets mangled — but the notice names it, and this matches the pipeline's existing behavior for results. - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1410
- **Title**: fix(1408): harness-induced bench failures — isolated job logs, redacted at rest, shape-only bash interceptor (AC1–AC3; AC4 documented)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1408-bench-harness-artifacts` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 27
- **Additions**: +1116
- **Deletions**: -29
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T11:25:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T20:46:35Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1408 (harness ACs). Bench-autopsy r3, run 37736364517: **~half of the non-stall failures were harness-induced, not agent failures.** This PR fixes the harness side (AC1–AC3) and root-causes AC4 with no code change, as the AC directs.

## AC1 — bench/unattended artifacts leave the task workspace
Evidence (H1, CONFIRMED ×2): `sanitize-git-repo`/`.hard` passed both secret tests and failed ONLY `test_no_other_files_changed` — fa's bash-job logs at `<task-cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs/` captured raw secrets from the agent's own greps; the agent sanitized its own harness logs; the extra modified files flipped the graded diff. The session root was already outside (`--session-root /agent-logs|/logs/agent/fah-sessions`); job logs were not.

- `ShellJobRegistry.jobLogDir` (default unchanged: `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs`), resolved at boot from `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR` (`jobLogDirOverride`; lib/ stays dart:io-free, the executable passes `Platform.environment`).
- The terminal-bench and harbor adapters export `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR=/tmp/fa-harness-artifacts/bash_jobs` — the in-container twin of $RUNNER_TEMP (pinned by a python UT on both adapters' env).
- UT: a run with the override leaves **no `.fah/` in the task dir** after completion; default location pinned for compat.

## AC2 — job logs redacted at rest
Evidence (H1): the logs are documented as NOT redacted and leaked real dataset secrets onto shared runners. Every detached job's log writes now pass through a line-buffered `JobLogRedactor` (new, `lib/src/env/`) **before** the size ceiling, so the resting file carries `[REDACTED:<kind>]` markers; a secret split across stream chunks still masks and the settle path flushes the trailing partial line. The CLI wires the same `RedactionPipeline` that masks tool results into the registry; the option forwards through every options rewrap (secrets/session-vars/cwd decorators, cube sandbox). The live output stream stays raw (transient; feeds the password detector) — at-rest is the contract, and `bash_job output` tails the redacted file.

- UTs: registry-level and LocalShell-level — a job echoing a fixture AWS access key leaves the marker on disk, never the secret; registered non-vendor secrets mask; no-redactor hosts keep byte-identical logs.

## AC3 — the interceptor never rewrites agent-authored identifiers
Evidence (H2, CONFIRMED): `configure-git-webserver` — the transcript records *"The literal key filename got mangled by a filter — I'll use a different key name."* A filter rewrote text inside a FILENAME the agent was creating; the agent found out via I/O errors.

- New `redactBashCommandSecretShapes` (`lib/src/approval/bash_shape_redaction.dart`): **only a recognized secret SHAPE** — a vendor token regex match (AWS `AKIA+16`, GitHub `ghp_`, OpenAI `sk-`, JWT, …) — is ever rewritten to `[REDACTED:<kind>]`. Key-like-but-unmatched text (random filenames, entropy-heavy identifiers, hex runs) stays byte-identical: no heuristic ever mutates agent-authored command text.
- The bash tool executes the rewritten command and prefixes the tool result with a notice **naming exactly what changed** (count + every shape label) on all three paths (foreground, yield-job, background) — the agent sees the rewrite instead of discovering corruption by failure.
- UTs: (a) a command creating a file whose name contains a key-like token is NOT rewritten (and runs byte-identically, no notice); (b) a true secret shape IS rewritten and the notice names it.

## AC4 — H4 root cause: no propagation bug; prompt-contract candidate (no code, per the AC)
Traced the full env path for the `create-bucket` trial: `LocalShell._environment` = `{...Platform.environment, ...?given}` — ambient env is inherited, `ShellExecOptions.env` overrides, never replaces (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`; pinned by the existing UT `env overrides merge over the host environment` in `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`). Every decorator (secrets, session-vars, cwd) merges additively; the bash tool passes no env; the adapters launch fa via docker-exec/tmux inside the task container, so compose-level task env reaches fa's process and its bash children. There is no env filtering/allowlist anywhere in the exec path. Conclusion: the creds the agent failed to find were **genuinely absent from that trial's container** (agent checked `aws configure list` + env, asked via request_secret, was declined unattended, stopped cleanly) — a task-side provisioning gap, not an fa bug. Documented as a **prompt-contract candidate**: "hunt credentials in common places (~/.aws/, /run/secrets/*, task files, metadata endpoints, localstack endpoint env) before declaring them missing", pairing with #1407's repeat-unresolved audit (H3's crashing test belongs there too).

## Tests
TDD; test files mirror lib/ structure (`test/approval/bash_shape_redaction_test.dart`, `test/tools/shell_jobs_isolation_test.dart`, groups in `test/env/shell_job_io_test.dart`, `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest` in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`). New code stays well under the 2800-line ceiling (largest touched file 1333 lines) and every new method is small (CC ≤ 8) and covered. Python suite: 234 tests, 1 pre-existing env failure unrelated to this branch (`test_sitecustomize` needs py≥3.10 `assertNoLogs`). Dart VM is unavailable in this lane (SIGKILLed) — changes verified by close reading; the gate re-runs in CI.

Fixes #1408

+/// Secret-SHAPE redaction for agent-authored `bash` command text (issue
+/// #1408 AC3).
+///
+/// The bench autopsy (run 37736364517, `configure-git-webserver`) recorded
+/// the agent's own words: *"The literal key filename got mangled by a
+/// filter — I'll use a different key name."* A filter had rewritten text
+/// inside a FILENAME the agent was creating; the agent discovered the
+/// corruption via I/O errors and planned around a filesystem being edited
+/// under it.
+///
+/// The contract after the fix:
+///
+/// - ONLY a recognized secret SHAPE — a vendor token regex match (AWS
+///   `AKIA…`, GitHub `ghp_…`, OpenAI `sk-…`, JWT, …) — is ever rewritten.
+///   Key-like text that matches no shape (random filenames, entropy-heavy
+///   identifiers, hex runs) stays byte-identical: agent-authored command
+///   text is never touched on a heuristic.
+/// - Every forced rewrite produces a [BashCommandRewrite.notice] naming
+///   exactly what changed; the bash tool surfaces it in the tool result so
+///   the agent sees the rewrite instead of discovering it by failure.
+///
+/// Pure and synchronous: [layerVendor] does the detection, this module only
+/// slices the command around the (non-overlapping, position-sorted)
+/// matches.
+library;
+
+import '../redact/layer_vendor.dart';
+import '../redact/redaction_types.dart';
+
+/// One rewritten span: the matched secret shape and where it sat in the
+/// ORIGINAL command text.
+final class BashCommandShapeChange {
+  /// The change record.
+  const BashCommandShapeChange({
+    required this.label,
+    required this.start,
+    required this.end,
+  });
+
+  /// The vendor kind label (e.g. `AWS Access Key`) — the name the notice
+  /// reports.
+  final String label;
+
+  /// Start offset of the original span.
+  final int start;
+
+  /// End offset (exclusive) of the original span.
+  final int end;
+}
+
+/// A rewritten bash command plus the record of every span that changed.
+final class BashCommandRewrite {
+  /// The rewrite result: [command] is what must execute/persist.
+  const BashCommandRewrite({required this.command, required this.changes});
+
+  /// The command text with every recognized secret shape replaced by its
+  /// `[REDACTED:<kind>]` marker.
+  final String command;
+
+  /// Every rewrite, in command order.
+  final List<BashCommandShapeChange> changes;
+
+  /// The tool-result notice naming exactly what changed (issue #1408 AC3):
+  /// count plus every rewritten shape's label, in order.
+  String get notice {
+    final labels = changes.map((change) => change.label).join(', ');
+    final n = changes.length;
+    return '[bash interceptor rewrote $n secret-shaped value'
+        '${n == 1 ? '' : 's'} in the command ($labels) — the executed '
+        'command carries the [REDACTED:…] markers; agent-authored text '
+        'that is not a recognized secret shape is never rewritten. Pass '
+        'the value as an env var (\$NAME) instead of literal text, or '
+        'register it with request_secret to have it passed verbatim.]';
+  }
+}
+
+/// Rewrites every recognized secret SHAPE in [command], or null when the
+/// command matches none — the common case, and the guarantee: key-like
+/// text without a full shape (filenames, identifiers) is never rewritten.
+///
+/// [config] selects the vendor layer (default: enabled, like the
+/// pipeline); a master-disabled config (`redact.enabled: false`) or one
+/// with the vendor layer off yields null — the same `redact:` section
+/// steers command rewriting and result/job-log masking (review
+/// 5456649624).
+///
+/// [approvedLiterals] are values the host registered as secrets (the
+/// `request_secret` tool, preconfig API keys → the pipeline's
+/// `registeredSecrets`): a match whose original text is one of them is
+/// left byte-identical so an approved value still materializes (the
+/// pipeline already masks it in transcripts). Without this escape hatch a
+/// credential-setup task would have no bash path for its own token
+/// (review 5456649624).
+BashCommandRewrite? redactBashCommandSecretShapes(
+  String command, {
+  RedactionConfig config = const RedactionConfig(),
+  Set<String> approvedLiterals = const {},
+}) {
+  final trimmed = command.trim();
+  if (trimmed.isEmpty ||
+      !config.enabled ||
+      !config.isLayerEnabled(RedactionLayer.vendor)) {
+    return null;
+  }
+  // layerVendor returns non-overlapping matches, but grouped per pattern —
+  // sort by position before slicing. Copy-free: on a quick-screen miss the
+  // layer returns a CONST (unmodifiable) empty list, so the emptiness check
+  // must precede any sort (issue #1408 red-head: sorting the const list
+  // crashed every bash call without a vendor-shaped substring).
+  final matches = layerVendor(command, config);
+  if (matches.isEmpty) return null;
+  matches.sort((a, b) => a.start.compareTo(b.start));
+  if (approvedLiterals.isNotEmpty) {
+    matches.removeWhere(
+      (match) => approvedLiterals.contains(
+        command.substring(match.start, match.end),
+      ),
+    );
+    if (matches.isEmpty) return null;
+  }
+  final buffer = StringBuffer();
+  final changes = <BashCommandShapeChange>[];
+  var cursor = 0;
+  for (final match in matches) {
+    buffer
+      ..write(command.substring(cursor, match.start))
+      ..write(redactionMarker(match.kindLabel));
+    changes.add(
+      BashCommandShapeChange(
+        label: match.kindLabel,
+        start: match.start,
+        end: match.end,
+      ),
+    );
+    cursor = match.end;
+  }
+  buffer.write(command.substring(cursor));
+  return BashCommandRewrite(command: buffer.toString(), changes: changes);
+}

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1410
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1410
- **Title**: fix(1408): harness-induced bench failures — isolated job logs, redacted at rest, shape-only bash interceptor (AC1–AC3; AC4 documented)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1408-bench-harness-artifacts` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 27
- **Additions**: +1116
- **Deletions**: -29
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T11:25:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T20:46:35Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1408 (harness ACs). Bench-autopsy r3, run 37736364517: **~half of the non-stall failures were harness-induced, not agent failures.** This PR fixes the harness side (AC1–AC3) and root-causes AC4 with no code change, as the AC directs.

## AC1 — bench/unattended artifacts leave the task workspace
Evidence (H1, CONFIRMED ×2): `sanitize-git-repo`/`.hard` passed both secret tests and failed ONLY `test_no_other_files_changed` — fa's bash-job logs at `<task-cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs/` captured raw secrets from the agent's own greps; the agent sanitized its own harness logs; the extra modified files flipped the graded diff. The session root was already outside (`--session-root /agent-logs|/logs/agent/fah-sessions`); job logs were not.

- `ShellJobRegistry.jobLogDir` (default unchanged: `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs`), resolved at boot from `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR` (`jobLogDirOverride`; lib/ stays dart:io-free, the executable passes `Platform.environment`).
- The terminal-bench and harbor adapters export `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR=/tmp/fa-harness-artifacts/bash_jobs` — the in-container twin of $RUNNER_TEMP (pinned by a python UT on both adapters' env).
- UT: a run with the override leaves **no `.fah/` in the task dir** after completion; default location pinned for compat.

## AC2 — job logs redacted at rest
Evidence (H1): the logs are documented as NOT redacted and leaked real dataset secrets onto shared runners. Every detached job's log writes now pass through a line-buffered `JobLogRedactor` (new, `lib/src/env/`) **before** the size ceiling, so the resting file carries `[REDACTED:<kind>]` markers; a secret split across stream chunks still masks and the settle path flushes the trailing partial line. The CLI wires the same `RedactionPipeline` that masks tool results into the registry; the option forwards through every options rewrap (secrets/session-vars/cwd decorators, cube sandbox). The live output stream stays raw (transient; feeds the password detector) — at-rest is the contract, and `bash_job output` tails the redacted file.

- UTs: registry-level and LocalShell-level — a job echoing a fixture AWS access key leaves the marker on disk, never the secret; registered non-vendor secrets mask; no-redactor hosts keep byte-identical logs.

## AC3 — the interceptor never rewrites agent-authored identifiers
Evidence (H2, CONFIRMED): `configure-git-webserver` — the transcript records *"The literal key filename got mangled by a filter — I'll use a different key name."* A filter rewrote text inside a FILENAME the agent was creating; the agent found out via I/O errors.

- New `redactBashCommandSecretShapes` (`lib/src/approval/bash_shape_redaction.dart`): **only a recognized secret SHAPE** — a vendor token regex match (AWS `AKIA+16`, GitHub `ghp_`, OpenAI `sk-`, JWT, …) — is ever rewritten to `[REDACTED:<kind>]`. Key-like-but-unmatched text (random filenames, entropy-heavy identifiers, hex runs) stays byte-identical: no heuristic ever mutates agent-authored command text.
- The bash tool executes the rewritten command and prefixes the tool result with a notice **naming exactly what changed** (count + every shape label) on all three paths (foreground, yield-job, background) — the agent sees the rewrite instead of discovering corruption by failure.
- UTs: (a) a command creating a file whose name contains a key-like token is NOT rewritten (and runs byte-identically, no notice); (b) a true secret shape IS rewritten and the notice names it.

## AC4 — H4 root cause: no propagation bug; prompt-contract candidate (no code, per the AC)
Traced the full env path for the `create-bucket` trial: `LocalShell._environment` = `{...Platform.environment, ...?given}` — ambient env is inherited, `ShellExecOptions.env` overrides, never replaces (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`; pinned by the existing UT `env overrides merge over the host environment` in `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`). Every decorator (secrets, session-vars, cwd) merges additively; the bash tool passes no env; the adapters launch fa via docker-exec/tmux inside the task container, so compose-level task env reaches fa's process and its bash children. There is no env filtering/allowlist anywhere in the exec path. Conclusion: the creds the agent failed to find were **genuinely absent from that trial's container** (agent checked `aws configure list` + env, asked via request_secret, was declined unattended, stopped cleanly) — a task-side provisioning gap, not an fa bug. Documented as a **prompt-contract candidate**: "hunt credentials in common places (~/.aws/, /run/secrets/*, task files, metadata endpoints, localstack endpoint env) before declaring them missing", pairing with #1407's repeat-unresolved audit (H3's crashing test belongs there too).

## Tests
TDD; test files mirror lib/ structure (`test/approval/bash_shape_redaction_test.dart`, `test/tools/shell_jobs_isolation_test.dart`, groups in `test/env/shell_job_io_test.dart`, `HarnessArtifactIsolationTest` in `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`). New code stays well under the 2800-line ceiling (largest touched file 1333 lines) and every new method is small (CC ≤ 8) and covered. Python suite: 234 tests, 1 pre-existing env failure unrelated to this branch (`test_sitecustomize` needs py≥3.10 `assertNoLogs`). Dart VM is unavailable in this lane (SIGKILLed) — changes verified by close reading; the gate re-runs in CI.

Fixes #1408
