    "description": "Fixes #1408 (harness ACs). Bench-autopsy r3, run 37736364517: **~half of the non-stall failures were harness-induced, not agent failures.** This PR fixes the harness side (AC1–AC3) and root-causes AC4 with no code change, as the AC directs.

## AC1 — bench/unattended artifacts leave the task workspace
Evidence (H1, CONFIRMED ×2): `sanitize-git-repo`/`.hard` passed both secret tests and failed ONLY `test_no_other_files_changed` — fa's bash-job logs at `<task-cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs/` captured raw secrets from the agent's own greps; the agent sanitized its own harness logs; the extra modified files flipped the graded diff. The session root was already outside (`--session-root /agent-logs|/logs/agent/fah-sessions`); job logs were not.

- `ShellJobRegistry.jobLogDir` (default unchanged: `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs`), resolved at boot from `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR` (`jobLogDirOverride`; lib/ stays dart:io-free, the executable passes `Platform.environment`).
- The terminal-bench and harbor adapters export `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR=/tmp/fa-harness-artifacts/bash_jobs` — the in-container twin of $RUNNER_TEMP (pinned by a python UT on both adapters' env).
- UT: a run with the override leaves **no `.fah/` in the task dir** after completion; default location pinned for compat.

## AC2 — job logs redacted at rest
Evidence (H1): the logs are documented as NOT redacted and leaked real dataset secrets onto shared runners. Every detached job's log writes now pass through a line-buffered `JobLogRedactor` (new, `lib/src/env/`) **before** the size ceiling, so the resting file carries `[REDACTED:<kind>]` markers; a secret split across stream chunks still masks and the settle path flushes the trailing partial line. The CLI wires the same `RedactionPipeline` that masks tool results into the registry; the option forwards through every options rewrap (secrets/session-vars/cwd decorators, cube sandbox). The live output stream stays raw (transient; feeds the password detector) — at-rest is the contract, and `bash_job output` tails the redacted file.

- UTs: registry-level and LocalShell-level — a job echoing a fixture AWS access key leaves the marker on disk, never the secret; registered non-vendor secrets mask; no-redactor hosts keep byte-identical logs.

## AC3 — the interceptor never rewrites agent-authored identifiers
Evidence (H2, CONFIRMED): `configure-git-webserver` — the transcript records *"The literal key filename got mangled by a filter — I'll use a different key name."* A filter rewrote text inside a FILENAME the agent was creating; the agent found out via I/O errors.

- New `redactBashCommandSecretShapes` (`lib/src/approval/bash_shape_redaction.dart`): **only a recognized secret SHAPE** — a vendor token regex match (AWS `AKIA+16`, GitHub `ghp_`, OpenAI `sk-`, JWT, …) — is ever rewritten to `[REDACTED:<kind>]`. Key-like-but-unmatched text (random filenames, entropy-heavy identifiers, hex runs) stays byte-identical: no heuristic ever mutates agent-authored command text.
- The bash tool executes the rewritten command and prefixes the tool result with a notice **naming exactly what changed** (count + every shape label) on all three paths (foreground, yield-job, background) — the agent sees the rewrite instead of discovering corruption by failure.
- UTs: (a) a command creating a file whose name contains a key-like token is NOT rewritten (and runs byte-identically, no notice); (b) a true secret shape IS rewritten and the notice names it.

Traced the full env path for the `create-bucket` trial: `LocalShell._environment` = `{...Platform.environment, ...?given}` — ambient env is inherited, `ShellExecOptions.env` overrides, never replaces (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`; pinned by the existing UT `env overrides merge over the host environment` in `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`). Every decorator (secrets, session-vars, cwd) merges additively; the bash tool passes no env; the adapters launch fa via docker-exec/tmux inside the task container, so compose-level task env reaches fa's process and its bash children. There is no env filtering/allowlist anywhere in the exec path. Conclusion: the creds the agent failed to find were **genuinely absent from that trial's container** (agent checked `aws configure list` + env, asked via request_secret, was declined unattended, stopped cleanly) — a task-side provisioning gap, not an fa bug. ## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench
  harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run under supervision,
  plus manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging — NO
  scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path. A proven flake (red in ≥2
  distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h) is quarantined via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json` (checked in, reviewed in the fix PR;
  `flake-watch.yml` files the issue and opens the PR) — the gate legs pipe
  their targets through `scripts/apply_quarantine.py`, while nightly
  KEEPS running the file to produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof.
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green
  (includes golden suite; integration-tagged `test/cli_visual` runs in the
  nightly workflow + on demand).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80% (full ratchet on main/nightly; PRs ratchet
  CHANGED lines via `scripts/diff_coverage.py`); jscpd duplication < 1%
  core `lib/`, < 3.7% `flutter_app/lib/` (ratchet — only tighten).
- Cross-module duplication (issue #487): clones spanning module roots
  (`lib`, `bin`, `flutter_app/lib`, `packages/*/lib`, `browser_ext/dart`)
  via `scripts/check_dup_cross_module.sh` — stage `dupx`, ONE jscpd
  invocation, marker-parity with the CI `guards` job (which also runs it
  for app-only PRs — cross-module clones are usually born app-side).
  Baseline 0.3013% of the combined ~283k lines, pinned 0.31 in
  `ci_fast_gate.sh` (ratchet — only tighten; the per-package gates above
  cannot see across module boundaries).
- CRAP ratchet (`crap4dart analyze`, tool pinned as
  `dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.11.0 <0.12.0"` — gh-1106
  superseded the old 0.10 bound; gates/baselines need 0.11), one config
  per package, thresholds are the current per-package max — only down
  from here:
  - core (`crap4dart.yaml`, sources `[lib, bin]`): **12.0** (issue #1234:
    the named census offenders moved — CC-12 trio + readPasteboardImage
    16.32 split, the 0%-cov CC-3 quartet and the named CC-9 tier covered
    or split, `_listModels` covered — but the first whole-tree
    measurement showed the 8.0 repin unearned: 54 methods at 12.00
    (CC-3@0% tier + covered CC-12 dispatchers) and 83 at 9.00. Threshold
    stays at the measured max; the tier is the next ladder card).

Then do my own fresh review of the current head for NEW issues:

Things to scrutinize:
a. `JobLogRedactor.ingest` — the overflow path: `_carry = ''` then `return transform(buffered) + _overflowMarker;`. Note buffered here is _carry + chunk. This force-flushes EVERYTHING including complete lines... fine, best-effort documented.

But there's a subtle issue: in the overflow path when `cut >= 0`? No wait — overflow only handled in the `cut < 0` branch. If buffered has a newline and is huge, the carry (`substring(cut+1)`) is bounded by the last line length — but a single line can still be > 1 MiB! Wait: if `cut >= 0`, `_carry = buffered.substring(cut + 1)` — that's the trailing partial line, which could be arbitrarily long if the chunk contains a newline early and then megabytes of text without another newline. Next ingest call: buffered = _carry (1 MiB+) + chunk... if again no newline, eventually > 1 MiB → force-flush. OK so the bound is enforced on the NEXT ingest, meaning the carry can temporarily exceed 1 MiB within a single ingest call (e.g., a chunk of 100 MiB containing a newline at position 0 and no more newlines: cut=0, carry = 100 MiB, returned). Hmm — the carry itself can exceed _maxCarryBytes after a single ingest. The force-flush only happens on the NEXT ingest call when there's no newline. Also at flush() time, the whole carry is transformed and returned — the return value flows into `_ceiling.ingest(rest)` which is a string in memory anyway. The memory bound: carry ≤ chunk size + prior carry. The chunk itself is already in memory (it came from the stream), so ingest doesn't grow memory beyond ~2x chunk size in the worst case within one call... Actually wait, no: carry grows ACROSS chunks. Each ingest concatenates _carry + chunk. If a job streams newline-free chunks of 64 KiB each, after 16 chunks buffered = 1 MiB → force-flush on the 17th. So the bound holds across chunks (carry ≤ 1 MiB + one chunk). Except the case above where a single chunk contains a newline followed by a huge tail — carry can be as big as one chunk. That's inherent (the chunk is already in memory), acceptable.

b. `fanOut` change: `final safe = _logBroken ? chunk : (_redactor?.ingest(chunk) ?? chunk); if (!_logBroken && safe.isNotEmpty)`. 

Subtle issue: if the redactor returns empty string (chunk fully buffered in carry), no write happens — correct. But there's an interplay with the size ceiling: `_ceiling.ingest(safe)` is called per-write. Previously every chunk fed the ceiling; now chunks swallowed by the carry don't. That's fine — bytes counted when actually written.

BUT: what about the ordering between the redactor's transform output and the ceiling's head/tail patching? Redaction shortens text (secrets → markers), so ceiling accounting is on redacted bytes. Fine.

Another subtle thing: the `_writeChain` async ordering vs `_carry` state mutation. `ingest` mutates `_carry` synchronously in fanOut (before the write chain resolves), and `flush()` is called in the settle path after `await _writeChain`. Since ingest is synchronous and always completes before flush (settle happens after streams close), the ordering is safe.

What about TWO concurrent fans? stdout and stderr — are they both routed through fanOut? Let me check the existing code in io_execution_env.dart. If stdout and stderr are separate streams each calling fanOut, and each has its own redactor? No — one shared `_redactor` for the job. Both streams' chunks flow through the same redactor sequentially (single isolate), so interleaving is handled by the line buffering (each chunk is processed atomically). A token split across a stdout-chunk boundary AND stderr interleaving... The carry joins consecutive chunks regardless of source; a secret split between stdout and stderr would be unusual. Fine.

c. The settle flush path: wrapped in try/on Object → `_logBroken = true`. Fine.

d. In `_awaitJobOutcome`, the rewrite notice now rides after truncation — good.

e. `redactBashCommandSecretShapes` — check `layerVendor` returns: the comment claims "on a quick-screen miss the layer returns a CONST (unmodifiable) empty list, so the emptiness check must precede any sort". Need to verify layerVendor's contract: does it ever return an unmodifiable non-empty list? If it returns growable lists per pattern merged... let me read layer_vendor.dart.

f. The `approvedLiterals` check uses `command.substring(match.start, match.end)` — exact-value comparison against registered secrets. Registered secrets are stored... in the pipeline's `registeredSecrets`. The CLI passes `config.redactionPipeline?.registeredSecrets.toSet()`. Is `registeredSecrets` a live list (getter returning unmodifiable view) or a copy? `.toSet()` copies — fine. "Live snapshot" claim: the closure `() => config.redactionPipeline?.registeredSecrets.toSet() ?? const {}` is evaluated per bash call — live. Good.

But one issue: the CLI passes `config.redactionPipeline?.config ?? const RedactionConfig(enabled: false)`. If redactionPipeline is null (redaction off), the config is disabled → no rewriting. If pipeline exists, its config is used. Consistent.

g. Security angle: the interceptor rewrites the command BEFORE execution. That means `echo <aws key>` now echoes the marker. Any false-positive risk: a command legitimately processing example keys (docs, tests) gets mangled — but the notice names it, and this matches the pipeline's existing behavior for results. Every detached job's log writes now pass through a line-buffered `JobLogRedactor` (new, `lib/src/env/`) **before** the size ceiling, so the resting file carries `[REDACTED:<kind>]` markers; a secret split across stream chunks still masks and the settle path flushes the trailing partial line. ## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench
  harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run under supervision,
  plus manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging — NO
  scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path. A proven flake (red in ≥2
  distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h) is quarantined via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json` (checked in, reviewed in the fix PR;
  `flake-watch.yml` files the issue and opens the PR) — the gate legs pipe
  their targets through `scripts/apply_quarantine.py`, while nightly
  KEEPS running the file to produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof.

But there's a subtle issue: in the overflow path when `cut >= 0`? No wait — overflow only handled in the `cut < 0` branch. If buffered has a newline and is huge, the carry (`substring(cut+1)`) is bounded by the last line length — but a single line can still be > 1 MiB! Wait: if `cut >= 0`, `_carry = buffered.substring(cut + 1)` — that's the trailing partial line, which could be arbitrarily long if the chunk contains a newline early and then megabytes of text without another newline. Next ingest call: buffered = _carry (1 MiB+) + chunk... if again no newline, eventually > 1 MiB → force-flush. OK so the bound is enforced on the NEXT ingest, meaning the carry can temporarily exceed 1 MiB within a single ingest call (e.g., a chunk of 100 MiB containing a newline at position 0 and no more newlines: cut=0, carry = 100 MiB, returned). Hmm — the carry itself can exceed _maxCarryBytes after a single ingest. The force-flush only happens on the NEXT ingest call when there's no newline. Also at flush() time, the whole carry is transformed and returned — the return value flows into `_ceiling.ingest(rest)` which is a string in memory anyway. The memory bound: carry ≤ chunk size + prior carry. The chunk itself is already in memory (it came from the stream), so ingest doesn't grow memory beyond ~2x chunk size in the worst case within one call... Actually wait, no: carry grows ACROSS chunks. Each ingest concatenates _carry + chunk. If a job streams newline-free chunks of 64 KiB each, after 16 chunks buffered = 1 MiB → force-flush on the 17th. So the bound holds across chunks (carry ≤ 1 MiB + one chunk). Except the case above where a single chunk contains a newline followed by a huge tail — carry can be as big as one chunk. That's inherent (the chunk is already in memory), acceptable.

Since ingest is synchronous and always completes before flush (settle happens after streams close), the ordering is safe.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard

  `flake-watch.yml` files the issue and opens the PR) — the gate legs pipe

  KEEPS running the file to produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof.

  nightly workflow + on demand).

This is a re-review cycle. The previous review (REQUEST_CHANGES) raised:
1. 🚨 BLOCKING: bash tool crash on sort of const [] — author claims fixed in 47b5356d1 (sort-guard: check isEmpty before sort)
2. 🚨 BLOCKING: test file doesn't compile — author claims fixed in 93ad382a4
3. 🚨 BLOCKING: AC1 CLI bookkeeping gap — author claims fixed in 9e1d8771a (`_jobBookkeepingDir` getter)
4. ⚠️ IMPORTANT: config-blind rewrite + no escape hatch — author claims fixed in f604134d6 (redactionConfig param + approvedSecretLiterals)
5. ⚠️ IMPORTANT: unbounded carry — author claims fixed in d6bf6a1f4 (1 MiB cap)
6. 💡 SUGGESTION: notice before truncation — author claims fixed in f604134d6
7. 💡 SUGGESTION: marker duplication — author claims fixed in f604134d6 (redactionMarker helper)
8. 💡 SUGGESTION: harbor adapter hardcoded path — author claims fixed in 9e1d8771a (_CONTAINER_JOB_LOG_DIR)
9. Non-blocking: flutter_app AgentService doesn't wire jobLogRedactor (AC2 parity) — is this fixed? Let me check.

My job now: verify all these fixes are actually present in the current diff, look for new issues, and produce the verdict. Let me verify each claim in the current checkout:

1. Sort-guard: VERIFIED in current code — `matches.isEmpty` check happens before `matches.sort`. And the comment says layerVendor returns const [] on quick-screen miss. But wait — is the list returned on a NON-miss (matches found) growable? `matches.sort` on a non-const list is fine if it's growable. Let me check layerVendor to see what it returns when there ARE matches — if it returns a `List.unmodifiable` or a const list in some other path, sort would still crash. Let me check layer_vendor.dart.

2. Analyzer issues in test file: current test file shows `String _textOf(...)` — fixed. `Result<ShellExecResult, ExecutionError> result = const Ok(...)` — fixed.

3. CLI bookkeeping: `_jobBookkeepingDir` getter now used for `_manifestPath`, `_withRegistryLock`, `_pruneOldJobLogs`. Fixed. But I should double-check: are there other places hardcoding `.fah/bash_jobs` in the CLI path? E.g., `captureLostJobs`, hub-mode `jobStarted`? The author says hub-mode jobStarted writes through the same `_manifestPath`. Let me grep.

4. redactionConfig + approvedSecretLiterals — verified in the diff above.

5. _maxCarryBytes cap — verified in job_log_redaction.dart.

6. Notice after truncation — verified in the diff (the `_awaitJobOutcome` change).

7. redactionMarker helper — verified in redaction_types.dart, used by pipeline and shape rewriter.

8. harbor _CONTAINER_JOB_LOG_DIR — verified in the diff.

9. flutter_app AgentService — need to check if it wires jobLogRedactor.

Then do my own fresh review of the current head for NEW issues:

Things to scrutinize:
a. `JobLogRedactor.ingest` — the overflow path: `_carry = ''` then `return transform(buffered) + _overflowMarker;`. Note buffered here is _carry + chunk. This force-flushes EVERYTHING including complete lines... fine, best-effort documented.

But there's a subtle issue: in the overflow path when `cut >= 0`? No wait — overflow only handled in the `cut < 0` branch. If buffered has a newline and is huge, the carry (`substring(cut+1)`) is bounded by the last line length — but a single line can still be > 1 MiB! Wait: if `cut >= 0`, `_carry = buffered.substring(cut + 1)` — that's the trailing partial line, which could be arbitrarily long if the chunk contains a newline early and then megabytes of text without another newline. Next ingest call: buffered = _carry (1 MiB+) + chunk... if again no newline, eventually > 1 MiB → force-flush. OK so the bound is enforced on the NEXT ingest, meaning the carry can temporarily exceed 1 MiB within a single ingest call (e.g., a chunk of 100 MiB containing a newline at position 0 and no more newlines: cut=0, carry = 100 MiB, returned). Hmm — the carry itself can exceed _maxCarryBytes after a single ingest. The force-flush only happens on the NEXT ingest call when there's no newline. Also at flush() time, the whole carry is transformed and returned — the return value flows into `_ceiling.ingest(rest)` which is a string in memory anyway. The memory bound: carry ≤ chunk size + prior carry. The chunk itself is already in memory (it came from the stream), so ingest doesn't grow memory beyond ~2x chunk size in the worst case within one call... Actually wait, no: carry grows ACROSS chunks. Each ingest concatenates _carry + chunk. If a job streams newline-free chunks of 64 KiB each, after 16 chunks buffered = 1 MiB → force-flush on the 17th. So the bound holds across chunks (carry ≤ 1 MiB + one chunk). Except the case above where a single chunk contains a newline followed by a huge tail — carry can be as big as one chunk. That's inherent (the chunk is already in memory), acceptable.

b. `fanOut` change: `final safe = _logBroken ? chunk : (_redactor?.ingest(chunk) ?? chunk); if (!_logBroken && safe.isNotEmpty)`. 

Subtle issue: if the redactor returns empty string (chunk fully buffered in carry), no write happens — correct. But there's an interplay with the size ceiling: `_ceiling.ingest(safe)` is called per-write. Previously every chunk fed the ceiling; now chunks swallowed by the carry don't. That's fine — bytes counted when actually written.

BUT: what about the ordering between the redactor's transform output and the ceiling's head/tail patching? Redaction shortens text (secrets → markers), so ceiling accounting is on redacted bytes. Fine.

Another subtle thing: the `_writeChain` async ordering vs `_carry` state mutation. `ingest` mutates `_carry` synchronously in fanOut (before the write chain resolves), and `flush()` is called in the settle path after `await _writeChain`. Since ingest is synchronous and always completes before flush (settle happens after streams close), the ordering is safe.

What about TWO concurrent fans? stdout and stderr — are they both routed through fanOut? Let me check the existing code in io_execution_env.dart. If stdout and stderr are separate streams each calling fanOut, and each has its own redactor? No — one shared `_redactor` for the job. Both streams' chunks flow through the same redactor sequentially (single isolate), so interleaving is handled by the line buffering (each chunk is processed atomically). A token split across a stdout-chunk boundary AND stderr interleaving... The carry joins consecutive chunks regardless of source; a secret split between stdout and stderr would be unusual. Fine.

c. The settle flush path: wrapped in try/on Object → `_logBroken = true`. Fine.

d. In `_awaitJobOutcome`, the rewrite notice now rides after truncation — good.

e. `redactBashCommandSecretShapes` — check `layerVendor` returns: the comment claims "on a quick-screen miss the layer returns a CONST (unmodifiable) empty list, so the emptiness check must precede any sort". Need to verify layerVendor's contract: does it ever return an unmodifiable non-empty list? If it returns growable lists per pattern merged... let me read layer_vendor.dart.

f. The `approvedLiterals` check uses `command.substring(match.start, match.end)` — exact-value comparison against registered secrets. Registered secrets are stored... in the pipeline's `registeredSecrets`. The CLI passes `config.redactionPipeline?.registeredSecrets.toSet()`. Is `registeredSecrets` a live list (getter returning unmodifiable view) or a copy? `.toSet()` copies — fine. "Live snapshot" claim: the closure `() => config.redactionPipeline?.registeredSecrets.toSet() ?? const {}` is evaluated per bash call — live. Good.

## AC1 — bench/unattended artifacts leave the task workspace
Evidence (H1, CONFIRMED ×2): `sanitize-git-repo`/`.hard` passed both secret tests and failed ONLY `test_no_other_files_changed` — fa's bash-job logs at `<task-cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs/` captured raw secrets from the agent's own greps; the agent sanitized its own harness logs; the extra modified files flipped the graded diff. The session root was already outside (`--session-root /agent-logs|/logs/agent/fah-sessions`); job logs were not.

- `ShellJobRegistry.jobLogDir` (default unchanged: `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs`), resolved at boot from `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR` (`jobLogDirOverride`; lib/ stays dart:io-free, the executable passes `Platform.environment`).

- UT: a run with the override leaves **no `.fah/` in the task dir** after completion; default location pinned for compat.

## AC2 — job logs redacted at rest
Evidence (H1): the logs are documented as NOT redacted and leaked real dataset secrets onto shared runners. Every detached job's log writes now pass through a line-buffered `JobLogRedactor` (new, `lib/src/env/`) **before** the size ceiling, so the resting file carries `[REDACTED:<kind>]` markers; a secret split across stream chunks still masks and the settle path flushes the trailing partial line. The CLI wires the same `RedactionPipeline` that masks tool results into the registry; the option forwards through every options rewrap (secrets/session-vars/cwd decorators, cube sandbox). The live output stream stays raw (transient; feeds the password detector) — at-rest is the contract, and `bash_job output` tails the redacted file.

- UTs: registry-level and LocalShell-level — a job echoing a fixture AWS access key leaves the marker on disk, never the secret; registered non-vendor secrets mask; no-redactor hosts keep byte-identical logs.

## AC3 — the interceptor never rewrites agent-authored identifiers
Evidence (H2, CONFIRMED): `configure-git-webserver` — the transcript records *"The literal key filename got mangled by a filter — I'll use a different key name."* A filter rewrote text inside a FILENAME the agent was creating; the agent found out via I/O errors.

- New `redactBashCommandSecretShapes` (`lib/src/approval/bash_shape_redaction.dart`): **only a recognized secret SHAPE** — a vendor token regex match (AWS `AKIA+16`, GitHub `ghp_`, OpenAI `sk-`, JWT, …) — is ever rewritten to `[REDACTED:<kind>]`. Key-like-but-unmatched text (random filenames, entropy-heavy identifiers, hex runs) stays byte-identical: no heuristic ever mutates agent-authored command text.
- The bash tool executes the rewritten command and prefixes the tool result with a notice **naming exactly what changed** (count + every shape label) on all three paths (foreground, yield-job, background) — the agent sees the rewrite instead of discovering corruption by failure.
- UTs: (a) a command creating a file whose name contains a key-like token is NOT rewritten (and runs byte-identically, no notice); (b) a true secret shape IS rewritten and the notice names it.

jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`

flutter analyze+tests;

a. `JobLogRedactor.ingest` — the overflow path: `_carry = ''` then `return transform(buffered) + _overflowMarker;`. Note buffered here is _carry + chunk. This force-flushes EVERYTHING including complete lines... fine, best-effort documented.

But there's a subtle issue: in the overflow path when `cut >= 0`? No wait — overflow only handled in the `cut < 0` branch. If buffered has a newline and is huge, the carry (`substring(cut+1)`) is bounded by the last line length — but a single line can still be > 1 MiB! Wait: if `cut >= 0`, `_carry = buffered.substring(cut + 1)` — that's the trailing partial line, which could be arbitrarily long if the chunk contains a newline early and then megabytes of text without another newline. Next ingest call: buffered = _carry (1 MiB+) + chunk... if again no newline, eventually > 1 MiB → force-flush. OK so the bound is enforced on the NEXT ingest, meaning the carry can temporarily exceed 1 MiB within a single ingest call (e.g., a chunk of 100 MiB containing a newline at position 0 and no more newlines: cut=0, carry = 100 MiB, returned). Hmm — the carry itself can exceed _maxCarryBytes after a single ingest. The force-flush only happens on the NEXT ingest call when there's no newline. Also at flush() time, the whole carry is transformed and returned — the return value flows into `_ceiling.ingest(rest)` which is a string in memory anyway. The chunk itself is already in memory (it came from the stream), so ingest doesn't grow memory beyond ~2x chunk size in the worst case within one call... Actually wait, no: carry grows ACROSS chunks. Each ingest concatenates _carry + chunk. If a job streams newline-free chunks of 64 KiB each, after 16 chunks buffered = 1 MiB → force-flush on the 17th. So the bound holds across chunks (carry ≤ 1 MiB + one chunk). Except the case above where a single chunk contains a newline followed by a huge tail — carry can be as big as one chunk. ## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench
  harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run under supervision,
  plus manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging — NO
  scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path. A proven flake (red in ≥2
  distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h) is quarantined via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json` (checked in, reviewed in the fix PR;
  `flake-watch.yml` files the issue and opens the PR) — the gate legs pipe
  their targets through `scripts/apply_quarantine.py`, while nightly
  KEEPS running the file to produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof.
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green
  (includes golden suite; integration-tagged `test/cli_visual` runs in the
  nightly workflow + on demand).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80% (full ratchet on main/nightly; PRs ratchet
  CHANGED lines via `scripts/diff_coverage.py`); jscpd duplication < 1%
  core `lib/`, < 3.7% `flutter_app/lib/` (ratchet — only tighten).

If buffered has a newline and is huge, the carry (`substring(cut+1)`) is bounded by the last line length — but a single line can still be > 1 MiB! ## AC2 — job logs redacted at rest
Evidence (H1): the logs are documented as NOT redacted and leaked real dataset secrets onto shared runners. Every detached job's log writes now pass through a line-buffered `JobLogRedactor` (new, `lib/src/env/`) **before** the size ceiling, so the resting file carries `[REDACTED:<kind>]` markers; a secret split across stream chunks still masks and the settle path flushes the trailing partial line. The CLI wires the same `RedactionPipeline` that masks tool results into the registry; the option forwards through every options rewrap (secrets/session-vars/cwd decorators, cube sandbox). The live output stream stays raw (transient; feeds the password detector) — at-rest is the contract, and `bash_job output` tails the redacted file.

## AC3 — the interceptor never rewrites agent-authored identifiers
Evidence (H2, CONFIRMED): `configure-git-webserver` — the transcript records *"The literal key filename got mangled by a filter — I'll use a different key name."* A filter rewrote text inside a FILENAME the agent was creating; the agent found out via I/O errors.

Key-like-but-unmatched text (random filenames, entropy-heavy identifiers, hex runs) stays byte-identical: no heuristic ever mutates agent-authored command text.
- The bash tool executes the rewritten command and prefixes the tool result with a notice **naming exactly what changed** (count + every shape label) on all three paths (foreground, yield-job, background) — the agent sees the rewrite instead of discovering corruption by failure.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files

Evidence (H1): the logs are documented as NOT redacted and leaked real dataset secrets onto shared runners. Every detached job's log writes now pass through a line-buffered `JobLogRedactor` (new, `lib/src/env/`) **before** the size ceiling, so the resting file carries `[REDACTED:<kind>]` markers; a secret split across stream chunks still masks and the settle path flushes the trailing partial line. Evidence (H2, CONFIRMED): `configure-git-webserver` — the transcript records *"The literal key filename got mangled by a filter — I'll use a different key name."* A filter rewrote text inside a FILENAME the agent was creating; the agent found out via I/O errors.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench
  harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run under supervision,
  plus manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging — NO
  scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path. A proven flake (red in ≥2
  distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h) is quarantined via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json` (checked in, reviewed in the fix PR;
  `flake-watch.yml` files the issue and opens the PR) — the gate legs pipe
  their targets through `scripts/apply_quarantine.py`, while nightly
  KEEPS running the file to produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof.

    "description": "Fixes #1408 (harness ACs). Bench-autopsy r3, run 37736364517: **~half of the non-stall failures were harness-induced, not agent failures.** This PR fixes the harness side (AC1–AC3) and root-causes AC4 with no code change, as the AC directs.

## AC1 — bench/unattended artifacts leave the task workspace
Evidence (H1, CONFIRMED ×2): `sanitize-git-repo`/`.hard` passed both secret tests and failed ONLY `test_no_other_files_changed` — fa's bash-job logs at `<task-cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs/` captured raw secrets from the agent's own greps; the agent sanitized its own harness logs; the extra modified files flipped the graded diff. The session root was already outside (`--session-root /agent-logs|/logs/agent/fah-sessions`); job logs were not.

- `ShellJobRegistry.jobLogDir` (default unchanged: `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs`), resolved at boot from `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR` (`jobLogDirOverride`; lib/ stays dart:io-free, the executable passes `Platform.environment`).
- The terminal-bench and harbor adapters export `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR=/tmp/fa-harness-artifacts/bash_jobs` — the in-container twin of $RUNNER_TEMP (pinned by a python UT on both adapters' env).
- UT: a run with the override leaves **no `.fah/` in the task dir** after completion; default location pinned for compat.

## AC2 — job logs redacted at rest
Evidence (H1): the logs are documented as NOT redacted and leaked real dataset secrets onto shared runners. Every detached job's log writes now pass through a line-buffered `JobLogRedactor` (new, `lib/src/env/`) **before** the size ceiling, so the resting file carries `[REDACTED:<kind>]` markers; a secret split across stream chunks still masks and the settle path flushes the trailing partial line. The CLI wires the same `RedactionPipeline` that masks tool results into the registry; the option forwards through every options rewrap (secrets/session-vars/cwd decorators, cube sandbox). The live output stream stays raw (transient; feeds the password detector) — at-rest is the contract, and `bash_job output` tails the redacted file.

- UTs: registry-level and LocalShell-level — a job echoing a fixture AWS access key leaves the marker on disk, never the secret; registered non-vendor secrets mask; no-redactor hosts keep byte-identical logs.

## AC3 — the interceptor never rewrites agent-authored identifiers
Evidence (H2, CONFIRMED): `configure-git-webserver` — the transcript records *"The literal key filename got mangled by a filter — I'll use a different key name."* A filter rewrote text inside a FILENAME the agent was creating; the agent found out via I/O errors.

- New `redactBashCommandSecretShapes` (`lib/src/approval/bash_shape_redaction.dart`): **only a recognized secret SHAPE** — a vendor token regex match (AWS `AKIA+16`, GitHub `ghp_`, OpenAI `sk-`, JWT, …) — is ever rewritten to `[REDACTED:<kind>]`. Key-like-but-unmatched text (random filenames, entropy-heavy identifiers, hex runs) stays byte-identical: no heuristic ever mutates agent-authored command text.
- The bash tool executes the rewritten command and prefixes the tool result with a notice **naming exactly what changed** (count + every shape label) on all three paths (foreground, yield-job, background) — the agent sees the rewrite instead of discovering corruption by failure.
- UTs: (a) a command creating a file whose name contains a key-like token is NOT rewritten (and runs byte-identically, no notice); (b) a true secret shape IS rewritten and the notice names it.

blocks.text:
## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench
  harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run under supervision,
  plus manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging — NO
  scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path. A proven flake (red in ≥2
  distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h) is quarantined via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json` (checked in, reviewed in the fix PR;
  `flake-watch.yml` files the issue and opens the PR) — the gate legs pipe
  their targets through `scripts/apply_quarantine.py`, while nightly
  KEEPS running the file to produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof.
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green
  (includes golden suite; integration-tagged `test/cli_visual` runs in the
  nightly workflow + on demand).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80% (full ratchet on main/nightly; PRs ratchet
  CHANGED lines via `scripts/diff_coverage.py`); jscpd duplication < 1%
  core `lib/`, < 3.7% `flutter_app/lib/` (ratchet — only tighten).
- Cross-module duplication (issue #487): clones spanning module roots
  (`lib`, `bin`, `flutter_app/lib`, `packages/*/lib`, `browser_ext/dart`)
  via `scripts/check_dup_cross_module.sh` — stage `dupx`, ONE jscpd
  invocation, marker-parity with the CI `guards` job (which also runs it
  for app-only PRs — cross-module clones are usually born app-side).
  Baseline 0.3013% of the combined ~283k lines, pinned 0.31 in
  `ci_fast_gate.sh` (ratchet — only tighten; the per-package gates above
  cannot see across module boundaries).
- CRAP ratchet (`crap4dart analyze`, tool pinned as
  `dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.11.0 <0.12.0"` — gh-1106
  superseded the old 0.10 bound; gates/baselines need 0.11), one config
  per package, thresholds are the current per-package max — only down
  from here:
  - core (`crap4dart.yaml`, sources `[lib, bin]`): **12.0** (issue #1234:
    the named census offenders moved — CC-12 trio + readPasteboardImage
    16.32 split, the 0%-cov CC-3 quartet and the named CC-9 tier covered
    or split, `_listModels` covered — but the first whole-tree
    measurement showed the 8.0 repin unearned: 54 methods at 12.00
    (CC-3@0% tier + covered CC-12 dispatchers) and 83 at 9.00. Threshold
    stays at the measured max; the tier is the next ladder card).

Key facts from AGENTS.md:
- `dart analyze` + dart format clean is a gate — BUT "Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files" — the hook self-heals formatting, and CI's static gate is `ci_fast_gate.sh`-based. Does CI fail on format? The hook self-heals before committing, so a pushed commit that is not format-clean means it was pushed without the hook... CI stages: "size+analyze" for docs; lib/bin/test → "+tests, coverage, CRAP, jscpd". The "dart analyze + dart format clean" bullet — is format part of CI's static gate? Let me check ci_fast_gate.sh quickly for the format stage.

Also validation CI (referee run 37788019242) ran GREEN 46/46 on content identical to this head per the author — meaning the CI's own gates (incl. static) passed on this content. If CI included a format gate, it passed... but locally `dart format` (SDK 3.13.5) reports 9 touched files not clean. Hmm — maybe CI's format stage uses a different dart version, or the CI format stage doesn't exist (hook-only extra!). The AGENTS.md says "Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files" — i.e., the format check is HOOK-ONLY, not a CI stage. That explains why validation CI can be green while files are not format-clean: the hook would have self-healed had the author committed with the hook; machine pushes bypass the hook.

So format-cleanliness is a SUGGESTION-level note (consistent with the previous round's adjudication: "the pre-commit self-heal will rewrite them on next touch").

And `dart analyze` IS a CI gate — it passed (referee green 46/46 + my local run clean of errors/warnings; the 3 infos don't fail analyze since infos aren't errors... `dart analyze` exit code is non-zero only for errors and warnings? Actually `dart analyze` exits non-zero if there are issues at the configured fatal level — default fatal is errors only... hmm, `dart analyze` returns exit code 1+ if any issues with severity >= warning? By default, infos don't fail. The repo may set fatal-infos in analysis_options? Let me check analysis_options.yaml quickly.

Also CRAP ratchet: new methods CC ≤ 8 claim; the PR description says under thresholds. Fine — CI covers.

blocks.text:
## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench
  harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run under supervision,
  plus manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging — NO
  scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path. A proven flake (red in ≥2
  distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h) is quarantined via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json` (checked in, reviewed in the fix PR;
  `flake-watch.yml` files the issue and opens the PR) — the gate legs pipe
  their targets through `scripts/apply_quarantine.py`, while nightly
  KEEPS running the file to produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof.
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green
  (includes golden suite; integration-tagged `test/cli_visual` runs in the
  nightly workflow + on demand).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80% (full ratchet on main/nightly; PRs ratchet
  CHANGED lines via `scripts/diff_coverage.py`); jscpd duplication < 1%
  core `lib/`, < 3.7% `flutter_app/lib/` (ratchet — only tighten).
- Cross-module duplication (issue #487): clones spanning module roots
  (`lib`, `bin`, `flutter_app/lib`, `packages/*/lib`, `browser_ext/dart`)
  via `scripts/check_dup_cross_module.sh` — stage `dupx`, ONE jscpd
  invocation, marker-parity with the CI `guards` job (which also runs it
  for app-only PRs — cross-module clones are usually born app-side).
  Baseline 0.3013% of the combined ~283k lines, pinned 0.31 in
  `ci_fast_gate.sh` (ratchet — only tighten; the per-package gates above
  cannot see across module boundaries).
- CRAP ratchet (`crap4dart analyze`, tool pinned as
  `dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.11.0 <0.12.0"` — gh-1106
  superseded the old 0.10 bound; gates/baselines need 0.11), one config
  per package, thresholds are the current per-package max — only down
  from here:
  - core (`crap4dart.yaml`, sources `[lib, bin]`): **12.0** (issue #1234:
    the named census offenders moved — CC-12 trio + readPasteboardImage
    16.32 split, the 0%-cov CC-3 quartet and the named CC-9 tier covered
    or split, `_listModels` covered — but the first whole-tree
    measurement showed the 8.0 repin unearned: 54 methods at 12.00
    (CC-3@0% tier + covered CC-12 dispatchers) and 83 at 9.00. Threshold
    stays at the measured max; the tier is the next ladder card).

Key facts from AGENTS.md:
- `dart analyze` + dart format clean is a gate — BUT "Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files" — the hook self-heals formatting, and CI's static gate is `ci_fast_gate.sh`-based. Does CI fail on format? The hook self-heals before committing, so a pushed commit that is not format-clean means it was pushed without the hook... CI stages: "size+analyze" for docs; lib/bin/test → "+tests, coverage, CRAP, jscpd". The "dart analyze + dart format clean" bullet — is format part of CI's static gate? Let me check ci_fast_gate.sh quickly for the format stage.

Also validation CI (referee run 37788019242) ran GREEN 46/46 on content identical to this head per the author — meaning the CI's own gates (incl. static) passed on this content. If CI included a format gate, it passed... but locally `dart format` (SDK 3.13.5) reports 9 touched files not clean. Hmm — maybe CI's format stage uses a different dart version, or the CI format stage doesn't exist (hook-only extra!). The AGENTS.md says "Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files" — i.e., the format check is HOOK-ONLY, not a CI stage. So format-cleanliness is a SUGGESTION-level note (consistent with the previous round's adjudication: "the pre-commit self-heal will rewrite them on next touch").

Actually `dart analyze` exits non-zero if there are issues at the configured fatal level — default fatal is errors only... hmm, `dart analyze` returns exit code 1+ if any issues with severity >= warning? By default, infos don't fail. The repo may set fatal-infos in analysis_options? Let me check analysis_options.yaml quickly.

blocks.text:
## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench
  harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run under supervision,
  plus manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging — NO
  scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path. A proven flake (red in ≥2
  distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h) is quarantined via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json` (checked in, reviewed in the fix PR;
  `flake-watch.yml` files the issue and opens the PR) — the gate legs pipe
  their targets through `scripts/apply_quarantine.py`, while nightly
  KEEPS running the file to produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof.
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green
  (includes golden suite; integration-tagged `test/cli_visual` runs in the
  nightly workflow + on demand).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80% (full ratchet on main/nightly; PRs ratchet
  CHANGED lines via `scripts/diff_coverage.py`); jscpd duplication < 1%
  core `lib/`, < 3.7% `flutter_app/lib/` (ratchet — only tighten).
- Cross-module duplication (issue #487): clones spanning module roots
  (`lib`, `bin`, `flutter_app/lib`, `packages/*/lib`, `browser_ext/dart`)
  via `scripts/check_dup_cross_module.sh` — stage `dupx`, ONE jscpd
  invocation, marker-parity with the CI `guards` job (which also runs it
  for app-only PRs — cross-module clones are usually born app-side).
  Baseline 0.3013% of the combined ~283k lines, pinned 0.31 in
  `ci_fast_gate.sh` (ratchet — only tighten; the per-package gates above
  cannot see across module boundaries).
- CRAP ratchet (`crap4dart analyze`, tool pinned as
  `dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.11.0 <0.12.0"` — gh-1106
  superseded the old 0.10 bound; gates/baselines need 0.11), one config
  per package, thresholds are the current per-package max — only down
  from here:
  - core (`crap4dart.yaml`, sources `[lib, bin]`): **12.0** (issue #1234:
    the named census offenders moved — CC-12 trio + readPasteboardImage
    16.32 split, the 0%-cov CC-3 quartet and the named CC-9 tier covered
    or split, `_listModels` covered — but the first whole-tree
    measurement showed the 8.0 repin unearned: 54 methods at 12.00
    (CC-3@0% tier + covered CC-12 dispatchers) and 83 at 9.00. Threshold
    stays at the measured max; the tier is the next ladder card).

Key facts from AGENTS.md:
- `dart analyze` + dart format clean is a gate — BUT "Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files" — the hook self-heals formatting, and CI's static gate is `ci_fast_gate.sh`-based. Does CI fail on format? The hook self-heals before committing, so a pushed commit that is not format-clean means it was pushed without the hook... CI stages: "size+analyze" for docs; lib/bin/test → "+tests, coverage, CRAP, jscpd". The "dart analyze + dart format clean" bullet — is format part of CI's static gate? Let me check ci_fast_gate.sh quickly for the format stage.

Also validation CI (referee run 37788019242) ran GREEN 46/46 on content identical to this head per the author — meaning the CI's own gates (incl. static) passed on this content. If CI included a format gate, it passed... but locally `dart format` (SDK 3.13.5) reports 9 touched files not clean. Hmm — maybe CI's format stage uses a different dart version, or the CI format stage doesn't exist (hook-only extra!). The AGENTS.md says "Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files" — i.e., the format check is HOOK-ONLY, not a CI stage. That explains why validation CI can be green while files are not format-clean: the hook would have self-healed had the author committed with the hook; machine pushes bypass the hook.

So format-cleanliness is a SUGGESTION-level note (consistent with the previous round's adjudication: "the pre-commit self-heal will rewrite them on next touch").

And `dart analyze` IS a CI gate — it passed (referee green 46/46 + my local run clean of errors/warnings; the 3 infos don't fail analyze since infos aren't errors... `dart analyze` exit code is non-zero only for errors and warnings? Actually `dart analyze` exits non-zero if there are issues at the configured fatal level — default fatal is errors only... hmm, `dart analyze` returns exit code 1+ if any issues with severity >= warning? By default, infos don't fail. The repo may set fatal-infos in analysis_options? Let me check analysis_options.yaml quickly.

Also CRAP ratchet: new methods CC ≤ 8 claim; the PR description says under thresholds. Fine — CI covers.

    "description": "Fixes #1408 (harness ACs). Bench-autopsy r3, run 37736364517: **~half of the non-stall failures were harness-induced, not agent failures.** This PR fixes the harness side (AC1–AC3) and root-causes AC4 with no code change, as the AC directs.

## AC1 — bench/unattended artifacts leave the task workspace
Evidence (H1, CONFIRMED ×2): `sanitize-git-repo`/`.hard` passed both secret tests and failed ONLY `test_no_other_files_changed` — fa's bash-job logs at `<task-cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs/` captured raw secrets from the agent's own greps; the agent sanitized its own harness logs; the extra modified files flipped the graded diff. The session root was already outside (`--session-root /agent-logs|/logs/agent/fah-sessions`); job logs were not.

- `ShellJobRegistry.jobLogDir` (default unchanged: `<cwd>/.fah/bash_jobs`), resolved at boot from `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR` (`jobLogDirOverride`; lib/ stays dart:io-free, the executable passes `Platform.environment`).
- The terminal-bench and harbor adapters export `FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR=/tmp/fa-harness-artifacts/bash_jobs` — the in-container twin of $RUNNER_TEMP (pinned by a python UT on both adapters' env).
- UT: a run with the override leaves **no `.fah/` in the task dir** after completion; default location pinned for compat.

## AC2 — job logs redacted at rest
Evidence (H1): the logs are documented as NOT redacted and leaked real dataset secrets onto shared runners. Every detached job's log writes now pass through a line-buffered `JobLogRedactor` (new, `lib/src/env/`) **before** the size ceiling, so the resting file carries `[REDACTED:<kind>]` markers; a secret split across stream chunks still masks and the settle path flushes the trailing partial line. The CLI wires the same `RedactionPipeline` that masks tool results into the registry; the option forwards through every options rewrap (secrets/session-vars/cwd decorators, cube sandbox). The live output stream stays raw (transient; feeds the password detector) — at-rest is the contract, and `bash_job output` tails the redacted file.

- UTs: registry-level and LocalShell-level — a job echoing a fixture AWS access key leaves the marker on disk, never the secret; registered non-vendor secrets mask; no-redactor hosts keep byte-identical logs.

## AC3 — the interceptor never rewrites agent-authored identifiers
Evidence (H2, CONFIRMED): `configure-git-webserver` — the transcript records *"The literal key filename got mangled by a filter — I'll use a different key name."* A filter rewrote text inside a FILENAME the agent was creating; the agent found out via I/O errors.

- New `redactBashCommandSecretShapes` (`lib/src/approval/bash_shape_redaction.dart`): **only a recognized secret SHAPE** — a vendor token regex match (AWS `AKIA+16`, GitHub `ghp_`, OpenAI `sk-`, JWT, …) — is ever rewritten to `[REDACTED:<kind>]`. Key-like-but-unmatched text (random filenames, entropy-heavy identifiers, hex runs) stays byte-identical: no heuristic ever mutates agent-authored command text.
- The bash tool executes the rewritten command and prefixes the tool result with a notice **naming exactly what changed** (count + every shape label) on all three paths (foreground, yield-job, background) — the agent sees the rewrite instead of discovering corruption by failure.
- UTs: (a) a command creating a file whose name contains a key-like token is NOT rewritten (and runs byte-identically, no notice); (b) a true secret shape IS rewritten and the notice names it.

## AC4 — H4 root cause: no propagation bug; prompt-contract candidate (no code, per the AC)
Traced the full env path for the `create-bucket` trial: `LocalShell._environment` = `{...Platform.environment, ...?given}` — ambient env is inherited, `ShellExecOptions.env` overrides, never replaces (`lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`; pinned by the existing UT `env overrides merge over the host environment` in `test/env/io_execution_env_test.dart`). Every decorator (secrets, session-vars, cwd) merges additively; the bash tool passes no env; the adapters launch fa via docker-exec/tmux inside the task container, so compose-level task env reaches fa's process and its bash children. There is no env filtering/allowlist anywhere in the exec path. Conclusion: the creds the agent failed to find were **genuinely absent from that trial's container** (agent checked `aws configure list` + env, asked via request_secret, was declined unattended, stopped cleanly) — a task-side provisioning gap, not an fa bug. Documented as a **prompt-contract candidate**: "hunt credentials in common places (~/.aws/, /run/secrets/*, task files, metadata endpoints, localstack endpoint env) before declaring them missing", pairing with #1407's repeat-unresolved audit (H3's crashing test belongs there too).

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench
  harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run under supervision,
  plus manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging — NO
  scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path. A proven flake (red in ≥2
  distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h) is quarantined via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json` (checked in, reviewed in the fix PR;
  `flake-watch.yml` files the issue and opens the PR) — the gate legs pipe
  their targets through `scripts/apply_quarantine.py`, while nightly
  KEEPS running the file to produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof.
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green
  (includes golden suite; integration-tagged `test/cli_visual` runs in the
  nightly workflow + on demand).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80% (full ratchet on main/nightly; PRs ratchet

  core `lib/`, < 3.7% `flutter_app/lib/` (ratchet — only tighten).

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
